# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/

## Commits and releases

- Commit identity: human/AI contributors commit as `ai.teammate
  <agent.ai.native@gmail.com>` (history was rewritten to it — set
  `git config user.name ai.teammate` + `git config user.email
  agent.ai.native@gmail.com` repo-locally). Release TAGS from
  `scripts/auto_release.sh` are authored `fa-release-bot[bot]
  <fa-release-bot[bot]@users.noreply.github.com>` — the gh-1172 App pushes
  the annotated tag, so the App identity is what auditability hangs on.
  gh-1402 rule: ANY automation that commits/pushes release-path changes
  (store metadata fixes, release tags/releases) MUST use the fa-release-bot
  GitHub App token — never a PAT, never the default `GITHUB_TOKEN`
  (main's required status checks reject both, #1098).
- Commit subjects: `type(scope): ...` (`feat:`, `fix:`, `fix(example):`,
  `ci:`, `test(providers):`, `refactor(prompts):`).
- Every push to `main` cuts an annotated TAG + GitHub Release
  (`scripts/auto_release.sh` via `ci.yml`) — ZERO commits land on main
  (gh-1522: the retired flow pushed a 4-file `chore(release):` bot commit
  per release). The git TAG is the single source of truth for versions:
  both pubspecs carry the FIXED `0.0.0-dev` placeholder (a hand-bump fails
  the Static `Version placeholder guard`), `pubspec.lock` never churns, and
  CI stamps the version at the edges: the `publish` job stamps the STAGED
  publish tree (pubspec version + generated changelog section prepend via
  `scripts/stamp_staged_release.sh`, staged version == tag guarded
  pre-upload), store/mobile builds stamp `--build-name/--build-number` from
  the derived tag version, `install_local.sh` stamps `version.txt` from

+/// The shared per-model context-window registry (gh-1742 invariant 2:
+/// ONE window per model identity, everywhere).
+///
+/// Today the resolved window lived only on the MAIN agent's `Model`
+/// instance: endpoint detection (`/models`) and `/model-edit` mutated that
+/// one instance, while every child resolved
+/// `effectiveContextWindow(wiring.model.contextWindow, null)` at spawn —
+/// a child spawned after a live detection still rode the stale catalog
+/// window (the dmtools evidence: children compacted at 88–97% of a
+/// 131,072-token window the same model really served at ≥478k). This
+/// registry is the ONE place a detection or override is published, keyed
+/// by the `(provider, modelId, baseUrl)` identity every provider request
+/// already rides, so main, children, the smol summarizer and the ctx
+/// meter resolve the same number (E2: a detection for one identity never
+/// crosses to another).
+///
+/// The registry also answers AC6's verified/unverified question: an entry
+/// means the window is backed by an endpoint report or a user pin; no
+/// entry means the carried (catalog) window is unverified and the meter
+/// marks it.
+library;
+
+import '../model.dart';
+
+/// The identity a context window is registered under: the same
+/// `(provider, modelId, baseUrl)` triple every provider request carries.
+final class ModelWindowKey {
+  /// Creates a key from explicit identity parts.
+  const ModelWindowKey({
+    required this.provider,
+    required this.modelId,
+    this.baseUrl,
+  });
+
+  /// Builds the key for [model] — provider case-folded, base URL
+  /// trailing-slash-normalized (saved entries and pinned chains disagree
+  /// on the trailing slash routinely; they are the same endpoint).
+  factory ModelWindowKey.of(Model model) => ModelWindowKey(
+    provider: model.provider.trim().toLowerCase(),
+    modelId: model.id.trim(),
+    baseUrl: _normalizeBaseUrl(model.baseUrl),
+  );
+
+  static String? _normalizeBaseUrl(String url) {
+    var normalized = url.trim();
+    while (normalized.endsWith('/')) {
+      normalized = normalized.substring(0, normalized.length - 1);
+    }
+    return normalized.isEmpty ? null : normalized;
+  }
+
+  /// The provider id (`openrouter`, `copilot`, …), case-folded.
+  final String provider;
+
+  /// The model id (`claude-sonnet-5-5`, `anthropic/…` on OpenRouter).
+  final String modelId;
+
+  /// The endpoint base URL, trailing-slash-normalized; null for blank.
+  final String? baseUrl;
+
+  @override
+  bool operator ==(Object other) =>
+      other is ModelWindowKey &&
+      other.provider == provider &&
+      other.modelId == modelId &&
+      other.baseUrl == baseUrl;
+
+  @override
+  int get hashCode => Object.hash(provider, modelId, baseUrl);
+
+  @override
+  String toString() => '$provider/$modelId@$baseUrl';
+}
+
+/// Where a registered window came from — the AC6 verification ladder:
+/// an endpoint report or a user pin VERIFIES the window; the absence of
+/// both leaves the carried (catalog) value unverified.
+enum ContextWindowSource {
+  /// The provider's `/models`-family endpoint reported the window.
+  endpointReport,
+
+  /// The user pinned the window explicitly (`/model-edit`, a roles-chain
+  /// entry) — wins over an endpoint report by publish order.
+  userPin,
+}
+
+/// One registered window with its provenance.
+final class RegisteredContextWindow {
+  /// Creates a registration row.
+  const RegisteredContextWindow({
+    required this.window,
+    required this.source,
+    required this.at,
+  });
+
+  /// The registered context window, in tokens.
+  final int window;
+
+  /// What backed the value ([ContextWindowSource]).
+  final ContextWindowSource source;
+
+  /// When the value was published.
+  final DateTime at;
+}
+
+/// The per-model window registry. One instance per session, shared by the
+/// host (main + meter), the task executor (children) and any other
+/// consumer of the effective window for a model identity.
+final class ContextWindowRegistry {
+  final Map<ModelWindowKey, RegisteredContextWindow> _entries = {};
+
+  /// Publishes [window] for [model]'s identity. Later publishes win (an
+  /// endpoint detection at boot, then a live `/model-edit`). Non-positive
+  /// windows are ignored — they are never a resolution.
+  void publish({
+    required Model model,
+    required int window,
+    required ContextWindowSource source,
+    DateTime? at,
+  }) {
+    if (window <= 0) return;
+    _entries[ModelWindowKey.of(model)] = RegisteredContextWindow(
+      window: window,
+      source: source,
+      at: at ?? DateTime.now(),
+    );
+  }
+
+  /// The registered window for [model]'s identity, or `null` when nothing
+  /// was published for it (the caller falls back to the carried value).
+  int? windowFor(Model model) => _entries[ModelWindowKey.of(model)]?.window;
+
+  /// Whether [model]'s window is backed by an endpoint report or a user
+  /// pin (AC6): `false` means the carried window is unverified and the
+  /// meters mark it.
+  bool isVerified(Model model) => _entries.containsKey(ModelWindowKey.of(model));
+
+  /// Drops every registration (test seam; a host never calls this
+  /// mid-session — E4 window shrinks arrive as new publishes).
+  void clear() => _entries.clear();
+
+  /// Read-only view for diagnostics/tests.
+  Map<ModelWindowKey, RegisteredContextWindow> get entries =>
+      Map.unmodifiable(_entries);
+}
+
+/// Returns [model] with its context window replaced by the registered
+/// value when one exists — the child-wiring shape of invariant 2 (the
+/// loop's over-window guard reads `model.contextWindow`, so the resolved
+/// window must ride the Model instance itself). Pure: returns [model]
+/// unchanged when nothing is registered or the value already matches.
+Model withRegisteredContextWindow(Model model, ContextWindowRegistry? registry) {
+  final registered = registry?.windowFor(model);
+  if (registered == null || registered == model.contextWindow) return model;
+  return Model(
+    id: model.id,
+    name: model.name,
+    api: model.api,
+    provider: model.provider,
+    baseUrl: model.baseUrl,
+    reasoning: model.reasoning,
+    input: model.input,
+    thinkingLevel: model.thinkingLevel,
+    cost: model.cost,

+    maxTokens: model.maxTokens,
+    headers: model.headers,
+    compat: model.compat,
+    authHeader: model.authHeader,
+    capabilityNotes: model.capabilityNotes,
+    connectTimeout: model.connectTimeout,
+    streamIdleTimeout: model.streamIdleTimeout,
+    timeoutScopeLabel: model.timeoutScopeLabel,
+  );

pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ### External-spec evidence rule A finding whose core claim is "**the spec / reference / ticket / external tool says or does X**" may be raised at 🚨 **BLOCKING** only when it quotes the exact source the review actually read during this run — a `file:line` reference or a doc URL. A bare "the spec says …" assertion is unfalsifiable for the author and for the machine, and a false one holds a validated PR hostage (live: a BLOCKING thread claiming an exemption list that the reference source did not contain — the reviewed code was behaviorally identical to it). Without a verifiable citation: - Downgrade the finding to ⚠️ **IMPORTANT**, phrased as a question: "Please confirm against `` — if confirmed, this becomes blocking." - Never let an uncited spec assertion be the sole reason for `REQUEST_CHANGES`. This is not a strictness cut: a spec-claim finding **with** a verifiable citation keeps full 🚨 BLOCKING force. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. # Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1753
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1753
- **Title**: gh-1742 [GOAL] Truthful context pressure: compaction keyed to observed usage + honest windows (subagents ride fictitious windows today)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1742` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 18
- **Additions**: +1738
- **Deletions**: -181
- **Created**: 2026-10-21T17:28:44Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-21T17:43:51Z

## PR Description

Closes #1742
### What changed
Context-pressure governance is now keyed to observed provider usage instead of the chars/4 estimate alone: pressure decisions reconcile `max(estimate, last observed input+cacheRead)`, all compaction surfaces resolve one shared per-model window registry, and headroom scales with the window instead of a flat 16k reserve.

### Key decisions
- New pure decision core `assessContextPressure` / `reconcileContextTokens` / `lastObservedContextTokens` (`lib/src/compaction/context_pressure.dart`): observed wins over estimate, estimate fills gaps; no observation yet = byte-identical legacy behavior.
- `ContextWindowRegistry` (`lib/src/compaction/context_window_registry.dart`): one window per `(provider, modelId, baseUrl)` shared by main, children, and the meter; `contextWindowCap` now applies to children too (previously `null` in `_compactChildIfNeeded`).
- `CompactionSettings.forWindow` proportional: reserve = `window/16` clamped to `[12.5k, 64k]`, keepRecent = `window/8` clamped to `[20k, 128k]` — a 1M window keeps ≥64k headroom instead of 1.6%. A legacy-parity floor (`min(4096, window/4)` for reserve, mirrored by keep) keeps the ≤64k band firing no later than before.
- The CLI joins the shared registry: `AgentCli` owns one, `_applyDetectedContextWindow` publishes endpoint reports, `/model-edit` publishes user pins, and `SubagentServices` hands it to the `task` tool — children spawned after a detection ride the served window, not the advertised one.
- Child compaction (`TaskExecutor._compactChildIfNeeded`): observed-over-headroom forces the pass through a per-child latch (`_forcedObservedAt`) so a stale pre-fold anchor cannot re-force every boundary.
- Fixed a real hole this exposed in `AutoCompactorFactory`: a FORCED structured run whose own estimate sat under the token trigger did zero passes yet reported `ok`, skipping the classic fallback — forced (usage- or message-cap-triggered) zero-pass outcomes now fall through to the classic engine, whose forced semantics actually run the summarizer.
- `SubagentHandle` pressure stamps carry `observedTokens` + `windowVerified` (AC6 badge basis for `task_status`).

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/compaction test/task test/agent test/cli
```

<details><summary>Verification notes</summary>

- `test/compaction test/task test/agent test/hosts`: 1204 passed, 0 failed. `test/cli`: 3920 passed, 6 skipped, 0 failed (including the resume-parity marathon set and HEP compaction frames).
- The shared `browser_ext`/`integration` suites (subprocess/PTY-heavy, outside this ticket's surface) show runner-load flakiness (subprocess 2-minute timeouts) on this shared runner; no gh-1742-touched path is involved — CI on the PR is the authoritative gate for those.
</details>

<details><summary>AC coverage</summary>

- **AC1/AC5** `test/compaction/context_pressure_test.dart` — reconciliation, forced-vs-estimate channels, edge `==` line.
- **AC2** `test/task/subagent_window_registry_test.dart` — registry published post-"detection" → child rides the registered window (131,072-vs-478k repro), cap clamps children.
- **AC2 (CLI)** `test/cli/agent_cli_context_window_registry_test.dart` — `/model-edit` publishes the pin; a child spawned after a registry entry resolves the registered window, not the carried one.
- **AC3** `test/compaction/compaction_test.dart` — reserve/keep tables 8k→2M, clamps, monotonicity, legacy-parity floor in the ≤64k band.
- **AC4/REG-1** `test/compaction/context_pressure_test.dart` — gh_1122 (never later than legacy at ≤200k) and kimi (−5% drift cannot delay the observed channel) regression pins at the real fixture scales.
- **AC5 IT** `test/task/subagent_window_registry_test.dart` — scripted gateway reporting `total_tokens` that excludes the cached prefix: estimate stays under the trigger while the forced pass demonstrably runs a compaction LLM call and lands a session compaction record.
</details>

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`

trajectory are SDK invariants with no override point (AC9). The
flutter_app is the second shell (slice 5): it wires through

## Commits and releases

- Commit identity: human/AI contributors commit as `ai.teammate
  <agent.ai.native@gmail.com>` (history was rewritten to it — set
  `git config user.name ai.teammate` + `git config user.email
  agent.ai.native@gmail.com` repo-locally). Release TAGS from
  `scripts/auto_release.sh` are authored `fa-release-bot[bot]
  <fa-release-bot[bot]@users.noreply.github.com>` — the gh-1172 App pushes
  the annotated tag, so the App identity is what auditability hangs on.
  gh-1402 rule: ANY automation that commits/pushes release-path changes
  (store metadata fixes, release tags/releases) MUST use the fa-release-bot
  GitHub App token — never a PAT, never the default `GITHUB_TOKEN`
  (main's required status checks reject both, #1098).
- Commit subjects: `type(scope): ...` (`feat:`, `fix:`, `fix(example):`,
  `ci:`, `test(providers):`, `refactor(prompts):`).
- Every push to `main` cuts an annotated TAG + GitHub Release
  (`scripts/auto_release.sh` via `ci.yml`) — ZERO commits land on main
  (gh-1522: the retired flow pushed a 4-file `chore(release):` bot commit
  per release). The git TAG is the single source of truth for versions:
  both pubspecs carry the FIXED `0.0.0-dev` placeholder (a hand-bump fails
  the Static `Version placeholder guard`), `pubspec.lock` never churns, and
  CI stamps the version at the edges: the `publish` job stamps the STAGED
  publish tree (pubspec version + generated changelog section prepend via
  `scripts/stamp_staged_release.sh`, staged version == tag guarded
  pre-upload), store/mobile builds stamp `--build-name/--build-number` from
  the derived tag version, `install_local.sh` stamps `version.txt` from
  `git describe`. CHANGELOG.md is curated-only: PRs add lines under
  `## Unreleased`; the release folds it into the tag's section AT STAGE
  TIME (`scripts/release_notes.sh` preference order: curated `## <version>`

  previous tag). The version scheme is `1.0.<counter>` (gh-785: App Store

  pre-flights the package-exists probe and exits 10 with the

+/// The shared per-model context-window registry (gh-1742 invariant 2:
+/// ONE window per model identity, everywhere).
+///
+/// Today the resolved window lived only on the MAIN agent's `Model`
+/// instance: endpoint detection (`/models`) and `/model-edit` mutated that
+/// one instance, while every child resolved
+/// `effectiveContextWindow(wiring.model.contextWindow, null)` at spawn —
+/// a child spawned after a live detection still rode the stale catalog
+/// window (the dmtools evidence: children compacted at 88–97% of a
+/// 131,072-token window the same model really served at ≥478k). This
+/// registry is the ONE place a detection or override is published, keyed
+/// by the `(provider, modelId, baseUrl)` identity every provider request
+/// already rides, so main, children, the smol summarizer and the ctx
+/// meter resolve the same number (E2: a detection for one identity never
+/// crosses to another).
+///
+/// The registry also answers AC6's verified/unverified question: an entry
+/// means the window is backed by an endpoint report or a user pin; no
+/// entry means the carried (catalog) window is unverified and the meter
+/// marks it.
+library;
+
+import '../model.dart';
+
+/// The identity a context window is registered under: the same
+/// `(provider, modelId, baseUrl)` triple every provider request carries.
+final class ModelWindowKey {
+  /// Creates a key from explicit identity parts.
+  const ModelWindowKey({
+    required this.provider,
+    required this.modelId,
+    this.baseUrl,
+  });
+
+  /// Builds the key for [model] — provider case-folded, base URL
+  /// trailing-slash-normalized (saved entries and pinned chains disagree
+  /// on the trailing slash routinely; they are the same endpoint).
+  factory ModelWindowKey.of(Model model) => ModelWindowKey(
+    provider: model.provider.trim().toLowerCase(),
+    modelId: model.id.trim(),
+    baseUrl: _normalizeBaseUrl(model.baseUrl),
+  );
+
+  static String? _normalizeBaseUrl(String url) {
+    var normalized = url.trim();
+    while (normalized.endsWith('/')) {
+      normalized = normalized.substring(0, normalized.length - 1);
+    }
+    return normalized.isEmpty ? null : normalized;
+  }
+
+  /// The provider id (`openrouter`, `copilot`, …), case-folded.
+  final String provider;
+
+  /// The model id (`claude-sonnet-5-5`, `anthropic/…` on OpenRouter).
+  final String modelId;
+
+  /// The endpoint base URL, trailing-slash-normalized; null for blank.
+  final String? baseUrl;
+
+  @override
+  bool operator ==(Object other) =>
+      other is ModelWindowKey &&
+      other.provider == provider &&
+      other.modelId == modelId &&
+      other.baseUrl == baseUrl;
+
+  @override
+  int get hashCode => Object.hash(provider, modelId, baseUrl);
+
+  @override
+  String toString() => '$provider/$modelId@$baseUrl';
+}
+
+/// Where a registered window came from — the AC6 verification ladder:
+/// an endpoint report or a user pin VERIFIES the window; the absence of
+/// both leaves the carried (catalog) value unverified.
+enum ContextWindowSource {
+  /// The provider's `/models`-family endpoint reported the window.
+  endpointReport,
+
+  /// The user pinned the window explicitly (`/model-edit`, a roles-chain
+  /// entry) — wins over an endpoint report by publish order.
+  userPin,
+}
+
+/// One registered window with its provenance.
+final class RegisteredContextWindow {
+  /// Creates a registration row.
+  const RegisteredContextWindow({
+    required this.window,
+    required this.source,
+    required this.at,
+  });
+
+  /// The registered context window, in tokens.
+  final int window;
+

+
+/// The per-model window registry. One instance per session, shared by the
+/// host (main + meter), the task executor (children) and any other
+/// consumer of the effective window for a model identity.
+final class ContextWindowRegistry {
+  final Map<ModelWindowKey, RegisteredContextWindow> _entries = {};
+
+  /// Publishes [window] for [model]'s identity. Later publishes win (an
+  /// endpoint detection at boot, then a live `/model-edit`). Non-positive
+  /// windows are ignored — they are never a resolution.
+  void publish({
+    required Model model,
+    required int window,
+    required ContextWindowSource source,
+    DateTime? at,
+  }) {
+    if (window <= 0) return;
+    _entries[ModelWindowKey.of(model)] = RegisteredContextWindow(
+      window: window,
+      source: source,
+      at: at ?? DateTime.now(),
+    );
+  }
+
+  /// The registered window for [model]'s identity, or `null` when nothing
+  /// was published for it (the caller falls back to the carried value).
+  int? windowFor(Model model) => _entries[ModelWindowKey.of(model)]?.window;
+
+  /// Whether [model]'s window is backed by an endpoint report or a user
+  /// pin (AC6): `false` means the carried window is unverified and the
+  /// meters mark it.
+  bool isVerified(Model model) => _entries.containsKey(ModelWindowKey.of(model));
+
+  /// Drops every registration (test seam; a host never calls this
+  /// mid-session — E4 window shrinks arrive as new publishes).
+  void clear() => _entries.clear();
+
+  /// Read-only view for diagnostics/tests.
+  Map<ModelWindowKey, RegisteredContextWindow> get entries =>
+      Map.unmodifiable(_entries);

+/// value when one exists — the child-wiring shape of invariant 2 (the
+/// loop's over-window guard reads `model.contextWindow`, so the resolved
+/// window must ride the Model instance itself). Pure: returns [model]
+/// unchanged when nothing is registered or the value already matches.
+Model withRegisteredContextWindow(Model model, ContextWindowRegistry? registry) {
+  final registered = registry?.windowFor(model);
+  if (registered == null || registered == model.contextWindow) return model;
+  return Model(

+    name: model.name,
+    api: model.api,
+    provider: model.provider,
+    baseUrl: model.baseUrl,
+    reasoning: model.reasoning,

- window=32768: legacy = 8192. New = max(2048, 4096) = 4096 → later. ✗
- window=49152: legacy = 12288. New = max(3072,4096)=4096 → later. ✗
- window=65536: legacy = 16384. New = max(4096,4096) = 4096 → later. ✗

So for windows strictly between 16,384 and 65,536 the claim "firing no later than before" is FALSE in the estimate-only channel. The floor `min(4096, window/4)` caps the floor at 4096, but legacy was window/4 up to 16384. The floor should be `min(16384, window/4)` to be legacy-parity (i.e., max(window/16, min(16384, window/4))). Hmm, but that would change 64k+ behavior... at 65536: min(16384, 16384) = 16384 → max(4096,16384) = 16384 = legacy. At 131072: min(16384, 32768) = 16384, max(8192, 16384) = 16384 = legacy. At 200k: min(16384, 500) = 16384, max(12500, 16384) = 16384 → still legacy flat. At 1M: max(65536, 16384) = 65536. Hmm, that construction would equal legacy up to... max(window/16, 16384) vs legacy min(16384, window/4)... crossover where window/16 ≥ 16384 → window ≥ 262144. So `max(window/16, min(16384, window/4))` would be exact legacy parity below 262144 and proportional above. The chosen `max(window/16, min(4096, window/4))` breaks parity in (16384, 262144) — firing later everywhere in that band (e.g., 200k: 12500 vs 16384).

Wait — is firing later a correctness bug or a design choice? The PR title says "no later than legacy" is REG-1's concern: gh-112's failure shape was a child riding an over-window context because compaction fired too late. The PR description says "keps the ≤64k band firing no later than before". The description text (the comment in code) claims ≤64k parity, which is false in (16k, 64k). But is this a *behavioral regression*? For estimate-only traffic on a 32k-window on-device model: legacy compacts when est > 24576; new compacts when est > 28672. Firing ~4k later on a small window. That eats 4k more of the window before compacting — for a 32k model that's 12.5% of the window. Could overflow? The reserve is the guard band for the summary prompt + output; a later trigger leaves less headroom for one huge tool result. There's also the loop's over-window guard as last resort. So it's a moderate drift, not a crash. But the claim in the code comment and PR description is inaccurate — worth an IMPORTANT finding (documentation/comment claims a parity guarantee that the formula doesn't deliver in (16k, 64k]).

Hold on. Let me double-check the claim once more. "keps the small-window band (≤64k, where `window/16` would undercut the flat legacy `min(16384, window/4)` reserve) firing no later than before". Maybe they mean: for windows ≤ 64k the floor `min(4096, window/4)`... no wait. Let me compute where window/16 < min(4096, window/4): window/16 < 4096 → window < 65536. And window/16 < window/4 always. So for window < 65536 the floor term min(4096, window/4) dominates when it exceeds window/16... The floor gives max(window/16, min(4096, window/4)). For window < 16384: window/4 < 4096, so floor = window/4 → reserve = max(window/16, window/4) = window/4 (for window ≥ 4096). Legacy = max(1024, window/4) = window/4. Parity below 16384. ✓.

For window in [16384, 65536): floor = 4096, reserve = max(window/16, 4096) = 4096 (window/16 ≤ 4096). Legacy = window/4 ∈ [4096, 16384]. So new reserve ≤ legacy, equality only at 16384. For window > 16384: strictly less → trigger strictly later. So the comment's claim is false for (16384, 65536). Actually — wait, I should double check: is firing "later" measured by trigger = window - reserve? Legacy trigger at 32768 = 32768-8192 = 24576. New trigger = 32768-4096 = 28672. Yes, later.

So: the comment and the test name 'the ≤64k band keeps the legacy flat reserve/keep ... small dev/on-device windows compact no later than before' — the test only checks 8192 and 16384, both of which happen to be exact-parity windows. The band (16k, 64k] is untested and breaks parity. The comment says "the floor is itself capped at `window/4`, so it fades out exactly where the proportional term takes over" — at 16384 floor = min(4096, 4096) = 4096 = window/4, and window/16 = 1024... they don't "fade out exactly where the proportional term takes over" — the proportional term takes over at 65536 (where window/16 = 4096). Between 16384 and 65536, the floor is flat-capped at 4096, which undercuts legacy's window/4 ramp.

Hmm, but hold on — for keepRecent: legacy keep = min(200, max(2048, window/2)). New keep = max(max(window/8, 2048), min(4096, window/2)) clamped to 131072. At window=16384: legacy keep = 8192; new = max(2048, min(4096,8192)) = 4096 < 8192. So keep HALVED at 16384. The test even pins this: `expect(s16384.keepRecentTokens, 4096)` — changed from 8192! So at 16384 the keep is NOT legacy parity either, and the test was CHANGED to accept the new value. The comment "small dev/on-device windows compact no later than before" (test comment) — keepRecent affects what's retained post-compaction, not the trigger. So keep halving at 16384 means after compaction less context is retained — a behavior change for small models. Not necessarily a bug, but it contradicts "byte-identical legacy behavior" claims? No — that claim was about pressure decision with no observation, not settings.

OK so this is a genuine doc-vs-code mismatch (comment claims parity band ≤64k; actual parity band is ≤16384 for reserve, and keep parity only ≤... let me compute keep crossover: legacy keep = min(200, max(2048, window/2)). New keep = min(131072, max(max(window/8,2048), min(4096, window/2)).
- window=8192: legacy = max(2048,4096)=4096; new = max(max(1024,2048), min(4096,4096)) = max(2048,4096)=4096. Equal.
- window=16384: legacy 8192; new 4096. Less.
So keep parity only ≤8192 (roughly). The changed test asserts the new value at 16384 without noting the behavior change.

Now — how severe? The AC3 doc in the PR description says: "A legacy-parity floor (`min(4096, window/4)` for reserve, mirrored by keep) keeps the ≤64k band firing no later than before." The formula `min(4096, window/4)`... hmm wait, maybe I'm misreading. For reserve the floor in code is `min(4096, window ~/ 4)`. Legacy reserve = `min(16384, max(1024, window ~/ 4))`. For window/4 ≤ 4096 (window ≤ 16384) the new floor = window/4 = legacy. Above 16384 legacy ramps beyond 4096, new caps at 4096. So the "legacy-parity floor" is only parity below 16384. The claim "keps the ≤64k band firing no later than before" is incorrect for (16k, 64k].

Actually, wait. Let me reconsider "firing no later than before" — with smaller reserve, trigger = window − reserve is HIGHER, so shouldCompact fires LATER (needs more tokens). Yes, later.

Is this a correctness issue (BLOCKING) or an IMPORTANT doc/comment issue? The behavior change: on windows in (16k, 64k], auto-compaction now fires later than the legacy behavior. The over-window guard remains. For a 64k window: legacy compacted at est > 49152; now at est > 6140. The reserve's purpose is to absorb the summarizer prompt+output. 4096 tokens for the summary prompt + output on a 64k window — the small-model justification. Hmm — this is likely a deliberate design choice (proportional headroom) with an inaccuracy in the justification narrative (the "parity" claim). The ticket (gh-1742) is about truthful pressure at large windows; the ≤64k band parity claim was probably intended to reassure no regression, and it's wrong in a 48k-wide band.

Given the verdict rules: BLOCKING = correctness/bug findings. A wrong code comment that mistates the guarantee + a test that pins values without noticing the parity break — I'd class the parity-claim mismatch as IMPORTANT (the formula is monotone, safe, and arguably intended; the *claim* is wrong). Actually wait — let me think about whether the actual firing behavior could regress gh-112's bug class (child rides over-window context). gh-112: children compacted at 88–97% of 131072 window — i.e., compaction happened too LATE, riding over. For a 131072 window: new reserve 8192 vs legacy 16384 → trigger at 12280 vs legacy 114688 — even later! 12280/131072 = 93.75% of the window before the estimate channel fires. The PR's own repro complaint was children compacting at 88–97% of window. The new formula makes the estimate channel fire at up to 93.75% on 128k windows — later than legacy's 87.5%. The mitigation is the observed channel (forced passes) — with a registry entry/detection the observed channel fires at window − reserve as well... observedTriggered: observed > window − reserve. Same line. So on 128k windows with no usage reporting (E1 degradation — providers without usage), the trigger is strictly later than legacy. That is a real regression of the guard band for the (16k, 262144) window range — including 128k/200k windows! At 200k: reserve 12500 vs 16384 → trigger 187500 vs 183616 — 3.9k later. The REG-1 test even acknowledges "the reconciled line (192,000) sits ABOVE the legacy line" and relies on the observed channel to fire earlier.

So the honest summary: the new settings deliberately reduce the reserve below legacy for windows in (16k, ~262k), moving the trigger later; the code comment + PR description + test names claim "no later than legacy" parity for ≤64k which is false. The saving grace is the observed channel — but it only exists when usage is reported (E1: gateways without usage reporting degrade to estimate-only, "exactly the legacy behavior" — which is now NOT true since settings changed for all windows!). That's the doc claim "no observation yet = byte-identical legacy behavior" — with no observation, assessContextPressure reduces to shouldCompact(pressure=est, window, settings) with settings = forWindow(window) which CHANGED. So "no observation yet = byte-identical legacy behavior" is false too: the trigger moved later for mid-size windows even estimate-only.

Hmm, "byte-identical legacy behavior" appears in the doc comment of context_pressure.dart: "Degradation (E1): no observation yet (fresh session) or a provider that reports no usable usage → estimate-only, exactly the legacy behavior." — "estimate-only, exactly the legacy behavior" refers to the reconciliation (no observed channel), and in isolation assessContextPressure with estimate-only = shouldCompact with the given settings. If the caller passes legacy settings, byte-identical. The statement is arguably scoped to the reconciliation layer. But combined with forWindow's change, end-to-end estimate-only behavior changed for windows in (16k, 262k). The regression risk: providers that don't report usage, mid-size windows — compaction fires later, closer to the hard window. The over-window guard (loop) is still there.

I'll classify: IMPORTANT (real behavior drift contradicting the PR's own parity claim + wrong comment/test narrative). Not BLOCKING since it doesn't break behavior outright — the trigger moving later by up to 12.3k tokens (at 200k) still leaves headroom proportional to window and the loop guard; and for the target 1M case it's a strict improvement. But hmm — for a 64k window, legacy fired at 49,152; new fires at 61,40. With reserve 4096 the summary must fit in 4096 tokens — the summarization payload budget is `sumarizationPayloadBudget(sumarizerWindow)` — separate. The reserve is about "summary prompt and its output" headroom — 4096 might be tight-ish but that's the design.

Wait, actually let me reconsider whether "no later than before" could refer to *the legacy-parity floor's effect*: i.e., "the floor keeps [the reserve] no smaller than [something] so firing happens no later". Since the floor fails to reach legacy values above 16384, firing is later. So the claim is just wrong in that band. Let me also check `keepRecent >= window` guard etc. Fine.

Let me also check monotonicity test: window 512 → ... step 512. forWindow(512): reserve = max(max(32,1024), min(4096,128)) = 1024; then reserve >= window/2 (256)? 1024 >= 256 → reserve = max(128,128) = 128. keep = max(max(64,2048), min(4096,256)) = 2048 >= 512 → keep = max(256, 256) = 256. OK.

Now the second big area: correctness of the forced latch in task_executor:

```dart
var runForced = false;
if (observed != null) {
 final latch = _forcedObservedAt[id];
 if (decision.nedsForce && (latch == null || observed > latch)) {
   _forcedObservedAt[id] = observed;
   runForced = true;
 } else if (!decision.observedTriggered && (latch == null || observed < latch)) {
   _forcedObservedAt[id] = observed;
 }
``

Scenario: observed = 130000 over the line → latch = 130000, runForced = true. Compaction runs, fold lands. Next boundary: observed still 130000 (stale anchor rides the kept tail? the kept tail after a fold includes recent messages whose usage rows are old? Actually after a fold, the transcript messages get replaced by a summary; the last assistant message usage — hmm, the fold keeps recent messages, which may include the assistant message carrying the 130000 usage). decision.nedsForce = true (observed > headroom line), latch == 130000, observed > latch false → runForced = false. But decision.triggered is still true (observedTriggered), so a compaction pass still runs — just not forced. Unforced pass → AutoCompactorFactory.run with force=false → structured engine gates on its own estimate → zero passes, ok → success short-circuit. Fine: no infinite forced loop, and the estimate channel would fire if the estimate crossed.

But wait — there's a subtle interplay with the AutoCompactorFactory zero-pass fix: if runForced=false but estimate under trigger, the structured engine does zero passes and returns ok → no classic fallback. Meanwhile observed is over the line but latched. Is that "relief"? The latch means: we already forced a pass at this observation level. After the forced pass, if the observation doesn't drop (because the fold kept the fat tail), we don't re-force. The comment explains this is deliberate ("a constant over-line observation must not re-run forced passes every boundary"). OK, deliberate.

Edge: observed rises but stays equal after a forced pass — e.g., observed 130000 forced, fold, next request reports 130000 again (kept tail + new turn ≈ same). latch == observed → not re-forced. Only strictly-greater re-forces. Deliberate.

Reset branch: `else if (!decision.observedTriggered && (latch == null || observed < latch))` — observed dropped under the line → latch = observed (lower). Next rise above the line re-forces since observed > latch. Correct-ish. Minor: when `decision.observedTriggered` is true but `observed <= latch` (no re-force), the latch stays. Fine.

One more check — `_forcedObservedAt` is a per-executor map keyed by child id; children are retained, ids stable across resume. Memory growth: bounded by number of children. OK.

Now — where does the executor pass `force: runForced`? In `_compactChildIfNeeded`, the AutoCompactorFactory is constructed with `force: runForced`. Let me read the current full function to make sure of the details, including what `est` is used for the factory.

Also check: `notePressure` now stamps `estTokens: reconcileContextTokens(...)` — the field is named estTokens but now carries reconciled pressure. task_status consumers... fine, documented.

Next, check `_childContextWindow`: `effectiveContextWindow(contextWindowRegistry?.windowFor(model) ?? model.contextWindow, contextWindowCap)`. And in `_resolveChildWiring`, the model gets `withRegisteredContextWindow`. But `_compactChildIfNeeded` uses `_childContextWindow(wiring.model)` where wiring.model is the resolved model — consistent.

But is there a path where the child's Model has the registered window applied (via withRegisteredContextWindow) AND the cap — while `_childContextWindow` re-aplies cap to the registry window? withRegisteredContextWindow doesn't apply the cap; the loop guard reads model.contextWindow directly. Hmm — the loop's over-window guard reads `model.contextWindow`; if the registry window (uncapped, e.g. 1M) is applied to the child model but the owner cap is 256k, then the loop guard divides by 1M while compaction uses `_childContextWindow` = effectiveContextWindow(1M, 256k) = 256k. Inconsistency! The comment in _resolveChildWiring says "the child loop's over-window guard and the compaction threshold divide by the same honest number". But withRegisteredContextWindow sets model.contextWindow = registered (uncapped), and _compactChildIfNeeded uses effectiveContextWindow(registry window, cap). If cap != null and cap > catalog but < registered, the guard basis (registered, 1M) and the compaction basis (capped 256k) differ — guard fires later than compaction. Let me check what effectiveContextWindow does and how the main agent resolves this for comparison. In the main agent, the CLI applies the cap to the main model's contextWindow? Let me check effectiveContextWindow and its callers.

Also: does the child model constructed by withRegisteredContextWindow need the cap applied to the Model itself for the guard? Let me look at how the main loop's guard works (agent_loop over-window guard) and how the CLI applies `contextWindowCap` to the main model. In AGENTS.md: "`agent:`/`contextWindowCap` ... SETS the EFFECTIVE context window via `effectiveContextWindow` (model.dart) for the compaction thresholds, the CLI ctx meter/footer and the loop's over-window guard — clamped down below the catalog window; raised above it". So for the MAIN agent, somewhere the cap is applied to the model instance or guard basis. Let me check.

Senior Code Reviewer & Security Expert ## agent_task_preamble.md You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ## review_coding_guidelines.md ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` ## general_guidelines.md # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,
ci_failures_full.log, pr_discussions.md,
pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. - **PR #**: 1753
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1753
- **Title**: gh-1742 [GOAL] Truthful context pressure: compaction keyed to observed usage + honest windows (subagents ride fictitious windows today)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1742` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 18
- **Additions**: +1738
- **Deletions**: -181
- **Created**: 2026-10-21T17:28:44Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-21T17:43:51Z

## PR Description

Closes #1742
### What changed
Context-pressure governance is now keyed to observed provider usage instead of the chars/4 estimate alone: pressure decisions reconcile `max(estimate, last observed input+cacheRead)`, all compaction surfaces resolve one shared per-model window registry, and headroom scales with the window instead of a flat 16k reserve.

### Key decisions
- New pure decision core `assessContextPressure` / `reconcileContextTokens` / `lastObservedContextTokens` (`lib/src/compaction/context_pressure.dart`): observed wins over estimate, estimate fills gaps; no observation yet = byte-identical legacy behavior.
- `ContextWindowRegistry` (`lib/src/compaction/context_window_registry.dart`): one window per `(provider, modelId, baseUrl)` shared by main, children, and the meter; `contextWindowCap` now applies to children too (previously `null` in `_compactChildIfNeeded`).
- `CompactionSettings.forWindow` proportional: reserve = `window/16` clamped to `[12.5k, 64k]`, keepRecent = `window/8` clamped to `[20k, 128k]` — a 1M window keeps ≥64k headroom instead of 1.6%. A legacy-parity floor (`min(4096, window/4)` for reserve, mirrored by keep) keeps the ≤64k band firing no later than before.
- The CLI joins the shared registry: `AgentCli` owns one, `_applyDetectedContextWindow` publishes endpoint reports, `/model-edit` publishes user pins, and `SubagentServices` hands it to the `task` tool — children spawned after a detection ride the served window, not the advertised one.
- Child compaction (`TaskExecutor._compactChildIfNeeded`): observed-over-headroom forces the pass through a per-child latch (`_forcedObservedAt`) so a stale pre-fold anchor cannot re-force every boundary.
- Fixed a real hole this exposed in `AutoCompactorFactory`: a FORCED structured run whose own estimate sat under the token trigger did zero passes yet reported `ok`, skipping the classic fallback — forced (usage- or message-cap-triggered) zero-pass outcomes now fall through to the classic engine, whose forced semantics actually run the summarizer.
- `SubagentHandle` pressure stamps carry `observedTokens` + `windowVerified` (AC6 badge basis for `task_status`).

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/compaction test/task test/agent test/cli
```

<details><summary>Verification notes</summary>

- `test/compaction test/task test/agent test/hosts`: 1204 passed, 0 failed. `test/cli`: 3920 passed, 6 skipped, 0 failed (including the resume-parity marathon set and HEP compaction frames).
- The shared `browser_ext`/`integration` suites (subprocess/PTY-heavy, outside this ticket's surface) show runner-load flakiness (subprocess 2-minute timeouts) on this shared runner; no gh-1742-touched path is involved — CI on the PR is the authoritative gate for those.
</details>

<details><summary>AC coverage</summary>

- **AC1/AC5** `test/compaction/context_pressure_test.dart` — reconciliation, forced-vs-estimate channels, edge `==` line.
- **AC2** `test/task/subagent_window_registry_test.dart` — registry published post-"detection" → child rides the registered window (131,072-vs-478k repro), cap clamps children.
- **AC2 (CLI)** `test/cli/agent_cli_context_window_registry_test.dart` — `/model-edit` publishes the pin; a child spawned after a registry entry resolves the registered window, not the carried one.
- **AC3** `test/compaction/compaction_test.dart` — reserve/keep tables 8k→2M, clamps, monotonicity, legacy-parity floor in the ≤64k band.
- **AC4/REG-1** `test/compaction/context_pressure_test.dart` — gh_1122 (never later than legacy at ≤200k) and kimi (−5% drift cannot delay the observed channel) regression pins at the real fixture scales.
- **AC5 IT** `test/task/subagent_window_registry_test.dart` — scripted gateway reporting `total_tokens` that excludes the cached prefix: estimate stays under the trigger while the forced pass demonstrably runs a compaction LLM call and lands a session compaction record.
</details>

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + one-shot note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist
  steering text after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on
  call+result). gh-1449: the drop note never costs the model a turn — it
  rides the payload's LAST existing user message as an extra text block
  (degenerate no-user-message payload degrades to the legacy standalone
  note), names tool/id/cut/kept-in-summary, and fires ONCE per orphan:
  `orphanReportKey` (canonical id + tool + timestamp) latches in
  `Agent.reportedOrphanKeys`; hosts persist each first-time batch as the
  hidden `orphan_report` custom record and seed the latch back at resume
  (CLI `_loadSession`, app `loadSession`).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail; its report carries `notedOrphanKeys` — the wire frame is
  optional-field backward-compatible); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run
  position-counter ids session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s
  `_localTrimFallback` routes the kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap
  (`images.maxPerRequest`, default 20) drops current-first-then-newest
  with a drop notice (never silent; the app logs drops via `AppLog`,
  issue #195 F4); dangling refs (compaction, cap) resolve to `(image no
  longer available)`, and once a renumbering boundary exists (compaction
  summary, structured marker, local-trim note) AUTHORED history
  citations degrade to that note too — after renumbering an `[Image N]`
  may name a different image, so silent rebinding is never allowed

across the core/task/extension surfaces at build time naming both

silently override SDK behavior, so the loud check lives in the builder,

wired profile hides from the registry with its reason surfaced on
`WiredAgentCore.extensions` (E8). The extension surface is additive-only:
memory, context management, compaction, the JSONL tool session and
trajectory are SDK invariants with no override point (AC9). The
flutter_app is the second shell (slice 5): it wires through
`flutterAppHostProfile` (lib/src/hosts/app_host_profile.dart — the app
host's own honest today-state, not the built-ins, whose cells pin the
matrix TARGET) and packages its platform tool families as a declared
`app-platform` extension — per-platform conditioning stays construction
glue in the shell, never a bare `if` around registration. Capabilities
the builder registers no tool for are declared with PRESENCE MARKER
services (`dynamicMessageSink`, `onDeviceProviderFactory`, the
`extRuntimeFactory` precedent): the host's extension carries the tool,
the marker keeps the cell honestly wired instead of run-narrowing off.
A host whose session scope differs from `ExecutionEnv.cwd` (the app's

workspace.

## Commits and releases

- Commit identity: human/AI contributors commit as `ai.teammate
  <agent.ai.native@gmail.com>` (history was rewritten to it — set
  `git config user.name ai.teammate` + `git config user.email
  agent.ai.native@gmail.com` repo-locally). Release TAGS from
  `scripts/auto_release.sh` are authored `fa-release-bot[bot]
  <fa-release-bot[bot]@users.noreply.github.com>` — the gh-1172 App pushes
  the annotated tag, so the App identity is what auditability hangs on.
  gh-1402 rule: ANY automation that commits/pushes release-path changes
  (store metadata fixes, release tags/releases) MUST use the fa-release-bot
  GitHub App token — never a PAT, never the default `GITHUB_TOKEN`
  (main's required status checks reject both, #1098).
- Commit subjects: `type(scope): ...` (`feat:`, `fix:`, `fix(example):`,
  `ci:`, `test(providers):`, `refactor(prompts):`).
- Every push to `main` cuts an annotated TAG + GitHub Release
  (`scripts/auto_release.sh` via `ci.yml`) — ZERO commits land on main
  (gh-1522: the retired flow pushed a 4-file `chore(release):` bot commit
  per release). The git TAG is the single source of truth for versions:
  both pubspecs carry the FIXED `0.0.0-dev` placeholder (a hand-bump fails
  the Static `Version placeholder guard`), `pubspec.lock` never churns, and
  CI stamps the version at the edges: the `publish` job stamps the STAGED
  publish tree (pubspec version + generated changelog section prepend via
  `scripts/stamp_staged_release.sh`, staged version == tag guarded
  pre-upload), store/mobile builds stamp `--build-name/--build-number` from
  the derived tag version, `install_local.sh` stamps `version.txt` from
  `git describe`. CHANGELOG.md is curated-only: PRs add lines under
  `## Unreleased`; the release folds it into the tag's section AT STAGE
  TIME (`scripts/release_notes.sh` preference order: curated `## <version>`
  section → curated `## Unreleased` body → conventional commits since the
  previous tag). The version scheme is `1.0.<counter>` (gh-785: App Store
  Connect approved 1.0.0 and enforces a monotonic
  `CFBundleShortVersionString`, so the pre-promotion `0.1.<counter>`
  train can never upload again). Release checklist: push to main (or the
  `releaseDispatch` dispatch) → watch the ci.yml `release` job cut the tag
  → watch the tag-scoped `publish` + `binaries` jobs. `fa --version` reads
  the stamped `version.txt` first, the placeholder pubspec second.
- `packages/fa_llm` publishes per `fa_llm-v*` tag via
  `.github/workflows/publish-fa-llm.yml` (OIDC, no secrets). First
  publish of a NEW package is manual — pub.dev OIDC only uploads new
  versions of an existing package (issue #1511): owner runs
  `cd packages/fa_llm && dart pub publish` once, adds the OIDC publisher
  entry on pub.dev, then the workflow takes over. The workflow
  pre-flights the package-exists probe and exits 10 with the
  instructions on 404; see `packages/fa_llm/README.md` §Publishing.
- CLI binaries build per tag (`ci.yml` `binaries` job), attach to the
  GitHub Release (`fa-<os>-<arch>[.exe]`); `installer-smoke` verifies
