+/// The shared per-model context-window registry (gh-1742 invariant 2:
+/// ONE window per model identity, everywhere).
+///
+/// Today the resolved window lived only on the MAIN agent's `Model`
+/// instance: endpoint detection (`/models`) and `/model-edit` mutated that
+/// one instance, while every child resolved
+/// `effectiveContextWindow(wiring.model.contextWindow, null)` at spawn —
+/// a child spawned after a live detection still rode the stale catalog
+/// window (the dmtools evidence: children compacted at 88–97% of a
+/// 131,072-token window the same model really served at ≥478k). This
+/// registry is the ONE place a detection or override is published, keyed
+/// by the `(provider, modelId, baseUrl)` identity every provider request
+/// already rides, so main, children, the smol summarizer and the ctx
+/// meter resolve the same number (E2: a detection for one identity never
+/// crosses to another).
+///
+/// The registry also answers AC6's verified/unverified question: an entry
+/// means the window is backed by an endpoint report or a user pin; no
+/// entry means the carried (catalog) window is unverified and the meter
+/// marks it.
+library;
+
+import '../model.dart';
+
+/// The identity a context window is registered under: the same
+/// `(provider, modelId, baseUrl)` triple every provider request carries.
+final class ModelWindowKey {
+  /// Creates a key from explicit identity parts.
+  const ModelWindowKey({
+    required this.provider,
+    required this.modelId,
+    this.baseUrl,
+  });
+
+  /// Builds the key for [model] — provider case-folded, base URL
+  /// trailing-slash-normalized (saved entries and pinned chains disagree
+  /// on the trailing slash routinely; they are the same endpoint).
+  factory ModelWindowKey.of(Model model) => ModelWindowKey(
+    provider: model.provider.trim().toLowerCase(),
+    modelId: model.id.trim(),
+    baseUrl: _normalizeBaseUrl(model.baseUrl),
+  );
+
+  static String? _normalizeBaseUrl(String url) {
+    var normalized = url.trim();
+    while (normalized.endsWith('/')) {
+      normalized = normalized.substring(0, normalized.length - 1);
+    }
+    return normalized.isEmpty ? null : normalized;
+  }
+
+  /// The provider id (`openrouter`, `copilot`, …), case-folded.
+  final String provider;
+
+  /// The model id (`claude-sonnet-5-5`, `anthropic/…` on OpenRouter).
+  final String modelId;
+
+  /// The endpoint base URL, trailing-slash-normalized; null for blank.
+  final String? baseUrl;
+
+  @override
+  bool operator ==(Object other) =>
+      other is ModelWindowKey &&
+      other.provider == provider &&
+      other.modelId == modelId &&
+      other.baseUrl == baseUrl;
+
+  @override
+  int get hashCode => Object.hash(provider, modelId, baseUrl);
+
+  @override
+  String toString() => '$provider/$modelId@$baseUrl';
+}
+
+/// Where a registered window came from — the AC6 verification ladder:
+/// an endpoint report or a user pin VERIFIES the window; the absence of
+/// both leaves the carried (catalog) value unverified.
+enum ContextWindowSource {
+  /// The provider's `/models`-family endpoint reported the window.
+  endpointReport,
+
+  /// The user pinned the window explicitly (`/model-edit`, a roles-chain
+  /// entry) — wins over an endpoint report by publish order.
+  userPin,
+}
+
+/// One registered window with its provenance.
+final class RegisteredContextWindow {
+  /// Creates a registration row.
+  const RegisteredContextWindow({
+    required this.window,
+    required this.source,
+    required this.at,
+  });
+
+  /// The registered context window, in tokens.
+  final int window;
+
+  /// What backed the value ([ContextWindowSource]).
+  final ContextWindowSource source;
+
+  /// When the value was published.
+  final DateTime at;
+}
+
+/// The per-model window registry. One instance per session, shared by the
+/// host (main + meter), the task executor (children) and any other
+/// consumer of the effective window for a model identity.
+final class ContextWindowRegistry {
+  final Map<ModelWindowKey, RegisteredContextWindow> _entries = {};
+
+  /// Publishes [window] for [model]'s identity. Later publishes win (an
+  /// endpoint detection at boot, then a live `/model-edit`). Non-positive
+  /// windows are ignored — they are never a resolution.
+  void publish({
+    required Model model,
+    required int window,
+    required ContextWindowSource source,
+    DateTime? at,
+  }) {
+    if (window <= 0) return;
+    _entries[ModelWindowKey.of(model)] = RegisteredContextWindow(
+      window: window,
+      source: source,
+      at: at ?? DateTime.now(),
+    );
+  }
+
+  /// The registered window for [model]'s identity, or `null` when nothing
+  /// was published for it (the caller falls back to the carried value).
+  int? windowFor(Model model) => _entries[ModelWindowKey.of(model)]?.window;
+
+  /// Whether [model]'s window is backed by an endpoint report or a user
+  /// pin (AC6): `false` means the carried window is unverified and the
+  /// meters mark it.
+  bool isVerified(Model model) => _entries.containsKey(ModelWindowKey.of(model));
+
+  /// Drops every registration (test seam; a host never calls this
+  /// mid-session — E4 window shrinks arrive as new publishes).
+  void clear() => _entries.clear();
+
+  /// Read-only view for diagnostics/tests.
+  Map<ModelWindowKey, RegisteredContextWindow> get entries =>
+      Map.unmodifiable(_entries);
+}
+
+/// Returns [model] with its context window replaced by the registered
+/// value when one exists — the child-wiring shape of invariant 2 (the
+/// loop's over-window guard reads `model.contextWindow`, so the resolved
+/// window must ride the Model instance itself). Pure: returns [model]
+/// unchanged when nothing is registered or the value already matches.
+Model withRegisteredContextWindow(Model model, ContextWindowRegistry? registry) {
+  final registered = registry?.windowFor(model);
+  if (registered == null || registered == model.contextWindow) return model;
+  return Model(
+    id: model.id,
+    name: model.name,
+    api: model.api,
+    provider: model.provider,
+    baseUrl: model.baseUrl,
+    reasoning: model.reasoning,
+    input: model.input,
+    thinkingLevel: model.thinkingLevel,
+    cost: model.cost,
+    contextWindow: registered,
+    maxTokens: model.maxTokens,
+    headers: model.headers,
+    compat: model.compat,
+    authHeader: model.authHeader,
+    capabilityNotes: model.capabilityNotes,
+    connectTimeout: model.connectTimeout,
+    streamIdleTimeout: model.streamIdleTimeout,
+    timeoutScopeLabel: model.timeoutScopeLabel,
+  );
+}

@@ -0,0 +1,175 @@
+/// The shared per-model context-window registry (gh-1742 invariant 2:
+/// ONE window per model identity, everywhere).
+///
+/// Today the resolved window lived only on the MAIN agent's `Model`
+/// instance: endpoint detection (`/models`) and `/model-edit` mutated that
+/// one instance, while every child resolved
+/// `effectiveContextWindow(wiring.model.contextWindow, null)` at spawn —
+/// a child spawned after a live detection still rode the stale catalog
+/// window (the dmtools evidence: children compacted at 88–97% of a
+/// 131,072-token window the same model really served at ≥478k). This
+/// registry is the ONE place a detection or override is published, keyed
+/// by the `(provider, modelId, baseUrl)` identity every provider request
+/// already rides, so main, children, the smol summarizer and the ctx
+/// meter resolve the same number (E2: a detection for one identity never
+/// crosses to another).
+///
+/// The registry also answers AC6's verified/unverified question: an entry
+/// means the window is backed by an endpoint report or a user pin; no
+/// entry means the carried (catalog) window is unverified and the meter
+/// marks it.
+library;
+
+import '../model.dart';
+
+/// The identity a context window is registered under: the same
+/// `(provider, modelId, baseUrl)` triple every provider request carries.
+final class ModelWindowKey {
+  /// Creates a key from explicit identity parts.
+  const ModelWindowKey({
+    required this.provider,
+    required this.modelId,
+    this.baseUrl,
+  });
+
+  /// Builds the key for [model] — provider case-folded, base URL
+  /// trailing-slash-normalized (saved entries and pinned chains disagree
+  /// on the trailing slash routinely; they are the same endpoint).
+  factory ModelWindowKey.of(Model model) => ModelWindowKey(
+    provider: model.provider.trim().toLowerCase(),
+    modelId: model.id.trim(),
+    baseUrl: _normalizeBaseUrl(model.baseUrl),
+  );
+
+  static String? _normalizeBaseUrl(String url) {
+    var normalized = url.trim();
+    while (normalized.endsWith('/')) {
+      normalized = normalized.substring(0, normalized.length - 1);
+    }
+    return normalized.isEmpty ? null : normalized;
+  }
+
+  /// The provider id (`openrouter`, `copilot`, …), case-folded.
+  final String provider;
+
+  /// The model id (`claude-sonnet-5-5`, `anthropic/…` on OpenRouter).
+  final String modelId;
+
+  /// The endpoint base URL, trailing-slash-normalized; null for blank.
+  final String? baseUrl;
+
+  @override
+  bool operator ==(Object other) =>
+      other is ModelWindowKey &&
+      other.provider == provider &&
+      other.modelId == modelId &&
+      other.baseUrl == baseUrl;
+
+  @override
+  int get hashCode => Object.hash(provider, modelId, baseUrl);
+
+  @override
+  String toString() => '$provider/$modelId@$baseUrl';
+}
+
+/// Where a registered window came from — the AC6 verification ladder:
+/// an endpoint report or a user pin VERIFIES the window; the absence of
+/// both leaves the carried (catalog) value unverified.
+enum ContextWindowSource {
+  /// The provider's `/models`-family endpoint reported the window.
+  endpointReport,
+
+  /// The user pinned the window explicitly (`/model-edit`, a roles-chain
+  /// entry) — wins over an endpoint report by publish order.
+  userPin,
+}
+
+/// One registered window with its provenance.
+final class RegisteredContextWindow {
+  /// Creates a registration row.
+  const RegisteredContextWindow({
+    required this.window,
+    required this.source,
+    required this.at,
+  });
+
+  /// The registered context window, in tokens.
+  final int window;
+
+  /// What backed the value ([ContextWindowSource]).
+  final ContextWindowSource source;
+
+  /// When the value was published.
+  final DateTime at;
+}
+
+/// The per-model window registry. One instance per session, shared by the
+/// host (main + meter), the task executor (children) and any other
+/// consumer of the effective window for a model identity.
+final class ContextWindowRegistry {
+  final Map<ModelWindowKey, RegisteredContextWindow> _entries = {};
+
+  /// Publishes [window] for [model]'s identity. Later publishes win (an
+  /// endpoint detection at boot, then a live `/model-edit`). Non-positive
+  /// windows are ignored — they are never a resolution.
+  void publish({
+    required Model model,
+    required int window,
+    required ContextWindowSource source,
+    DateTime? at,
+  }) {
+    if (window <= 0) return;
+    _entries[ModelWindowKey.of(model)] = RegisteredContextWindow(
+      window: window,
+      source: source,
+      at: at ?? DateTime.now(),
+    );
+  }
+
+  /// The registered window for [model]'s identity, or `null` when nothing
+  /// was published for it (the caller falls back to the carried value).
+  int? windowFor(Model model) => _entries[ModelWindowKey.of(model)]?.window;
+
+  /// Whether [model]'s window is backed by an endpoint report or a user
+  /// pin (AC6): `false` means the carried window is unverified and the
+  /// meters mark it.
+  bool isVerified(Model model) => _entries.containsKey(ModelWindowKey.of(model));
+
+  /// Drops every registration (test seam; a host never calls this
+  /// mid-session — E4 window shrinks arrive as new publishes).
+  void clear() => _entries.clear();
+
+  /// Read-only view for diagnostics/tests.
+  Map<ModelWindowKey, RegisteredContextWindow> get entries =>
+      Map.unmodifiable(_entries);
+}
+
+/// Returns [model] with its context window replaced by the registered
+/// value when one exists — the child-wiring shape of invariant 2 (the
+/// loop's over-window guard reads `model.contextWindow`, so the resolved
+/// window must ride the Model instance itself). Pure: returns [model]
+/// unchanged when nothing is registered or the value already matches.
+Model withRegisteredContextWindow(Model model, ContextWindowRegistry? registry) {
+  final registered = registry?.windowFor(model);
+  if (registered == null || registered == model.contextWindow) return model;
+  return Model(
+    id: model.id,
+    name: model.name,
+    api: model.api,
+    provider: model.provider,
+    baseUrl: model.baseUrl,
+    reasoning: model.reasoning,
+    input: model.input,
+    thinkingLevel: model.thinkingLevel,
+    cost: model.cost,
+    contextWindow: registered,
+    maxTokens: model.maxTokens,
+    headers: model.headers,
+    compat: model.compat,
+    authHeader: model.authHeader,
+    capabilityNotes: model.capabilityNotes,
+    connectTimeout: model.connectTimeout,
+    streamIdleTimeout: model.streamIdleTimeout,
+    timeoutScopeLabel: model.timeoutScopeLabel,
+  );
+}

blocks.text:
The child Agent doesn't get a `contextWindowCap` — the Agent class has no cap param presumably; the loop's guard reads `effectiveContextWindow(model.contextWindow, cap)` from its own config. For the child, the guard basis is `model.contextWindow` (cap = null, since the child loop config presumably has contextWindowCap null). So withRegisteredContextWindow puts the REGISTERED (uncapped) window on the child model — the child's over-window guard basis. Meanwhile `_compactChildIfNeeded` computes the compaction window as effectiveContextWindow(registry window, cap). If the owner cap RAISES... the cap can't raise above the registered window (cap raises above catalog but here the basis is already the registered/served window). If the cap clamps DOWN (cap < registered window), then: compaction basis = cap, guard basis = registered (uncapped). The guard fires later than compaction. Previously (before this PR): guard basis = model.contextWindow (catalog) and compaction basis = effectiveContextWindow(catalog, null) — consistent. Now with a registry entry + a clamp-down cap: compaction at 256k basis, guard at 1M. The compaction trigger (window−reserve at 256k) fires far before the guard at 1M — compaction is proactive anyway, so the guard lag is not harmful per se; guard is last resort. Actually wait, the inconsistency direction: compaction fires EARLIER than the guard. That's safe-ish (compaction is the mechanism; the guard is emergency). The comment in _resolveChildWiring claims "the child loop's over-window guard and the compaction threshold divide by the same honest number the main agent and the ctx meter resolve" — with a clamp-down cap they don't: guard rides the uncapped registered window, compaction the capped. Minor doc inaccuracy; behavior: compaction stays under the cap, guard lags — acceptable but the claim is inaccurate.

Hmm wait — actually which is "correct"? The owner cap says "treat the window as 256k" — the child compaction honors it (good, parity with main). The child guard sees 1M. If usage hits 300k (over the 256k cap), compaction should have fired at 240k (256k−16k). If compaction failed (best-effort), the guard wouldn't fire until 1M — riding way over the cap. Before the registry existed, guard = catalog 200k → guard fired at 200k. Now guard = registered 1M. Edge: registry publishes a raised window (endpoint report says 1M for a 200k-catalog id) + owner cap clamps to 256k + compaction repeatedly fails → the guard basis silently moved from 200k to 1M for children. The over-window guard is the "last resort" against provider hard-overflow; publishing a served-truth window SHOULD raise it (that's the point — the provider accepts 1M). But the owner explicitly capped at 256k — main's guard honors the cap (agent_loop uses cap), children's doesn't. So the child guard diverges from the main guard under a cap. That's a real, if edge-case, inconsistency: "the cap wins in whichever direction it points, same as the main agent" — for compaction, but NOT for the child loop guard (cap never reaches the child loop). Severity: IMPORTANT (edge case; compaction normally prevents reaching the guard).

Previously (before this PR): guard basis = model.contextWindow (catalog) and compaction basis = effectiveContextWindow(catalog, null) — consistent. Now with a registry entry + a clamp-down cap: compaction at 256k basis, guard at 1M. The compaction trigger (window−reserve at 256k) fires far before the guard at 1M — compaction is proactive anyway, so the guard lag is not harmful per se; guard is last resort. Actually wait, the inconsistency direction: compaction fires EARLIER than the guard. That's safe-ish (compaction is the mechanism; the guard is emergency). The comment in _resolveChildWiring claims "the child loop's over-window guard and the compaction threshold divide by the same honest number the main agent and the ctx meter resolve" — with a clamp-down cap they don't: guard rides the uncapped registered window, compaction the capped. Previously (before this PR): guard basis = model.contextWindow (catalog) and compaction basis = effectiveContextWindow(catalog, null) — consistent. Now with a registry entry + a clamp-down cap: compaction at 256k basis, guard at 1M. The compaction trigger (window−reserve at 256k) fires far before the guard at 1M — compaction is proactive anyway, so the guard lag is not harmful per se; guard is last resort. Interesting. Test at 16384: keepRecentTokens changed from 8192 to 4096. Let me verify: at window=16384, new keepRecent = min(131072, max(max(2048, 2048), min(4096, 8192))) = max(2048, 4096) = 4096. That contradicts the claim "keps the ≤64k band firing no later than before" — well, keepRecent affects the post-compaction kept region, not the trigger. But the reserve: at 16384 reserve is 4096 = legacy 4096. Equal. OK at 16k.

But between 16384 and 65536, the new reserve < legacy reserve (as I computed: at 20480, legacy 5120 vs new 4096; at 65536, legacy 16384 vs new 4096). And the comment says "keps the small-window band (≤64k...) firing no later than before". At 65536: legacy reserve = min(16384, 16384) = 16384; new = 4096. So the trigger boundary moves from 49152 to 6140 — firing LATER. The comment claim seems factually wrong for windows in (16384, 65536]. Hmm wait — "the ≤64k band" might mean windows ≤ 64k where... let me compute precisely the crossover where new reserve = legacy reserve:

legacy(window) = min(16384, max(1024, window/4)).
new(window) = min(65536, max(max(window/16, 1024), min(4096, window/4)).

For window ≥ 65536: window/16 ≥ 4096, so new = min(65536, max(window/16, ...)) = min(65536, max(window/16, 1024, min(4096,window/4))) = window/16 (since window/16 ≥ 4096 ≥ the others), clamped to 65536 at ≥1M. legacy at 65536..65536*... hmm legacy for window in [65536, 262144] = 16384 (min). new = window/16: at 131072 = 8192 < 16384 legacy! At 262144 = 16384 = legacy. At 2000: new = 12500 vs legacy 16384. So even at 200k, the new reserve (12500) < legacy (16384) → trigger fires LATER than legacy at 200k: legacy trigger = 2000-16384 = 183616; new trigger = 187500.

So the "gh_112 (never later than legacy at ≤200k)" claim — the PR description says "AC4/REG-1 ... gh_112 (never later than legacy at ≤200k)". But by the numbers, forWindow(2000).reserveTokens = 12500 < 16384 → the estimate-channel trigger crosses later than legacy. Unless the observed channel compensates. But the regression claim says "never later than legacy at ≤200k". Let me find the test.

Wait, that's contradictory reasoning: "the reconciled line sits ABOVE the legacy line, so with pressure = max(est,obs) the firing boundary can only be the same or earlier." If the line is ABOVE the legacy line, firing requires pressure > 192000 vs legacy pressure > 188416 — the new line fires LATER for a given pressure trajectory. The reason it doesn't fire later in this test is because pressure = max(est,obs) includes the observed channel that legacy didn't have. So the compound system fires earlier in practice, but the estimate-channel-only line moved LATER (192000 > 188416). The test name says "the reconciled trigger fires no later than legacy" — for this specific fixture with observed 199098 it fires. OK.

So the tests are honest about it. But the forWindow comment in compaction.dart says: "A legacy-parity floor keeps the small-window band (≤64k, where window/16 would undercut the flat legacy min(16384, window/4) reserve) firing no later than before". Let me verify this claim carefully at various windows ≤ 64k with no observations (estimate-only):

- window=8192: legacy reserve = min(16384, max(1024, 2048)) = 2048. New = min(65536, max(max(512,1024), min(4096,2048))) = max(1024, 2048) = 2048. Equal → parity.
- window=16384: legacy = min(16384, 4096) = 4096. New = max(max(1024,1024), min(4096,4096)) = 4096. Equal.
- window=20480: legacy = min(16384, 5120) = 5120. New = max(max(1280,1024), min(4096,5120)) = max(1280,4096) = 4096. NEW < LEGACY → fires LATER. ✗
- window=32768: legacy = 8192. New = max(2048, 4096) = 4096 → later. ✗
- window=49152: legacy = 12288. New = max(3072,4096)=4096 → later. ✗
- window=65536: legacy = 16384. New = max(4096,4096) = 4096 → later. ✗

So for windows strictly between 16,384 and 65,536 the claim "firing no later than before" is FALSE in the estimate-only channel. The floor `min(4096, window/4)` caps the floor at 4096, but legacy was window/4 up to 16384. The floor should be `min(16384, window/4)` to be legacy-parity (i.e., max(window/16, min(16384, window/4))). Hmm, but that would change 64k+ behavior... at 65536: min(16384, 16384) = 16384 → max(4096,16384) = 16384 = legacy. At 131072: min(16384, 32768) = 16384, max(8192, 16384) = 16384 = legacy. At 200k: min(16384, 500) = 16384, max(12500, 16384) = 16384 → still legacy flat. At 1M: max(65536, 16384) = 65536. Hmm, that construction would equal legacy up to... max(window/16, 16384) vs legacy min(16384, window/4)... crossover where window/16 ≥ 16384 → window ≥ 262144. So `max(window/16, min(16384, window/4))` would be exact legacy parity below 262144 and proportional above. The chosen `max(window/16, min(4096, window/4))` breaks parity in (16384, 262144) — firing later everywhere in that band (e.g., 200k: 12500 vs 16384).

Wait — is firing later a correctness bug or a design choice? The PR title says "no later than legacy" is REG-1's concern: gh-112's failure shape was a child riding an over-window context because compaction fired too late. The PR description says "keps the ≤64k band firing no later than before". The description text (the comment in code) claims ≤64k parity, which is false in (16k, 64k). But is this a *behavioral regression*? For estimate-only traffic on a 32k-window on-device model: legacy compacts when est > 24576; new compacts when est > 28672. Firing ~4k later on a small window. That eats 4k more of the window before compacting — for a 32k model that's 12.5% of the window. Could overflow? The reserve is the guard band for the summary prompt + output; a later trigger leaves less headroom for one huge tool result. There's also the loop's over-window guard as last resort. So it's a moderate drift, not a crash. But the claim in the code comment and PR description is inaccurate — worth an IMPORTANT finding (documentation/comment claims a parity guarantee that the formula doesn't deliver in (16k, 64k]).

Hold on. Let me double-check the claim once more. "keps the small-window band (≤64k, where `window/16` would undercut the flat legacy `min(16384, window/4)` reserve) firing no later than before". Maybe they mean: for windows ≤ 64k the floor `min(4096, window/4)`... no wait. Let me compute where window/16 < min(4096, window/4): window/16 < 4096 → window < 65536. And window/16 < window/4 always. So for window < 65536 the floor term min(4096, window/4) dominates when it exceeds window/16... The floor gives max(window/16, min(4096, window/4)). For window < 16384: window/4 < 4096, so floor = window/4 → reserve = max(window/16, window/4) = window/4 (for window ≥ 4096). Legacy = max(1024, window/4) = window/4. Parity below 16384. ✓.

For window in [16384, 65536): floor = 4096, reserve = max(window/16, 4096) = 4096 (window/16 ≤ 4096). Legacy = window/4 ∈ [4096, 16384]. So new reserve ≤ legacy, equality only at 16384. For window > 16384: strictly less → trigger strictly later. So the comment's claim is false for (16384, 65536). Actually — wait, I should double check: is firing "later" measured by trigger = window - reserve? Legacy trigger at 32768 = 32768-8192 = 24576. New trigger = 32768-4096 = 28672. Yes, later.

Now with a registry entry + a clamp-down cap: compaction at 256k basis, guard at 1M. The compaction trigger (window−reserve at 256k) fires far before the guard at 1M — compaction is proactive anyway, so the guard lag is not harmful per se; guard is last resort. The REG-1 gh_112 test acknowledges: "forWindow(204800).reserveTokens (12,800) < legacy 16,384 → the reconciled line (192,000) sits ABOVE the legacy line, so with pressure = max(est, obs) the firing boundary can only be the same or earlier."

Wait, that's contradictory reasoning: "the reconciled line sits ABOVE the legacy line, so with pressure = max(est,obs) the firing boundary can only be the same or earlier." If the line is ABOVE the legacy line, firing requires pressure > 192000 vs legacy pressure > 188416 — the new line fires LATER for a given pressure trajectory. The reason it doesn't fire later in this test is because pressure = max(est,obs) includes the observed channel that legacy didn't have. So the compound system fires earlier in practice, but the estimate-channel-only line moved LATER (192000 > 188416). The test name says "the reconciled trigger fires no later than legacy" — for this specific fixture with observed 199098 it fires. OK.

So the tests are honest about it. But the forWindow comment in compaction.dart says: "A legacy-parity floor keeps the small-window band (≤64k, where window/16 would undercut the flat legacy min(16384, window/4) reserve) firing no later than before". Let me verify this claim carefully at various windows ≤ 64k with no observations (estimate-only):

- window=8192: legacy reserve = min(16384, max(1024, 2048)) = 2048. New = min(65536, max(max(512,1024), min(4096,2048))) = max(1024, 2048) = 2048. Equal → parity.
- window=16384: legacy = min(16384, 4096) = 4096. New = max(max(1024,1024), min(4096,4096)) = 4096. Equal.
- window=20480: legacy = min(16384, 5120) = 5120. New = max(max(1280,1024), min(4096,5120)) = max(1280,4096) = 4096. NEW < LEGACY → fires LATER. ✗
- window=32768: legacy = 8192. New = max(2048, 4096) = 4096 → later. ✗
- window=49152: legacy = 12288. New = max(3072,4096)=4096 → later. ✗
- window=65536: legacy = 16384. New = max(4096,4096) = 4096 → later. ✗

So for windows strictly between 16,384 and 65,536 the claim "firing no later than before" is FALSE in the estimate-only channel. The floor `min(4096, window/4)` caps the floor at 4096, but legacy was window/4 up to 16384. The floor should be `min(16384, window/4)` to be legacy-parity (i.e., max(window/16, min(16384, window/4))). Hmm, but that would change 64k+ behavior... at 65536: min(16384, 16384) = 16384 → max(4096,16384) = 16384 = legacy. At 131072: min(16384, 32768) = 16384, max(8192, 16384) = 16384 = legacy. At 200k: min(16384, 500) = 16384, max(12500, 16384) = 16384 → still legacy flat. At 1M: max(65536, 16384) = 65536. Hmm, that construction would equal legacy up to... max(window/16, 16384) vs legacy min(16384, window/4)... crossover where window/16 ≥ 16384 → window ≥ 262144. So `max(window/16, min(16384, window/4))` would be exact legacy parity below 262144 and proportional above. The chosen `max(window/16, min(4096, window/4))` breaks parity in (16384, 262144) — firing later everywhere in that band (e.g., 200k: 12500 vs 16384).

Wait — is firing later a correctness bug or a design choice? The PR title says "no later than legacy" is REG-1's concern: gh-112's failure shape was a child riding an over-window context because compaction fired too late. The PR description says "keps the ≤64k band firing no later than before". The description text (the comment in code) claims ≤64k parity, which is false in (16k, 64k). But is this a *behavioral regression*? For estimate-only traffic on a 32k-window on-device model: legacy compacts when est > 24576; new compacts when est > 28672. Firing ~4k later on a small window. That eats 4k more of the window before compacting — for a 32k model that's 12.5% of the window. Could overflow? The reserve is the guard band for the summary prompt + output; a later trigger leaves less headroom for one huge tool result. There's also the loop's over-window guard as last resort. So it's a moderate drift, not a crash. But the claim in the code comment and PR description is inaccurate — worth an IMPORTANT finding (documentation/comment claims a parity guarantee that the formula doesn't deliver in (16k, 64k]).

Hold on. Let me double-check the claim once more. "keps the small-window band (≤64k, where `window/16` would undercut the flat legacy `min(16384, window/4)` reserve) firing no later than before". Maybe they mean: for windows ≤ 64k the floor `min(4096, window/4)`... no wait. Let me compute where window/16 < min(4096, window/4): window/16 < 4096 → window < 65536. And window/16 < window/4 always. So for window < 65536 the floor term min(4096, window/4) dominates when it exceeds window/16... The floor gives max(window/16, min(4096, window/4)). For window < 16384: window/4 < 4096, so floor = window/4 → reserve = max(window/16, window/4) = window/4 (for window ≥ 4096). Legacy = max(1024, window/4) = window/4. Parity below 16384. ✓.

For window in [16384, 65536): floor = 4096, reserve = max(window/16, 4096) = 4096 (window/16 ≤ 4096). Legacy = window/4 ∈ [4096, 16384]. So new reserve ≤ legacy, equality only at 16384. For window > 16384: strictly less → trigger strictly later. So the comment's claim is false for (16384, 65536). Actually — wait, I should double check: is firing "later" measured by trigger = window - reserve? Legacy trigger at 32768 = 32768-8192 = 24576. New trigger = 32768-4096 = 28672. Yes, later.

So: the comment and the test name 'the ≤64k band keeps the legacy flat reserve/keep ... small dev/on-device windows compact no later than before' — the test only checks 8192 and 16384, both of which happen to be exact-parity windows. The band (16k, 64k] is untested and breaks parity. The comment says "the floor is itself capped at `window/4`, so it fades out exactly where the proportional term takes over" — at 16384 floor = min(4096, 4096) = 4096 = window/4, and window/16 = 1024... they don't "fade out exactly where the proportional term takes over" — the proportional term takes over at 65536 (where window/16 = 4096). Between 16384 and 65536, the floor is flat-capped at 4096, which undercuts legacy's window/4 ramp.

So at 16384 the keep is NOT legacy parity either, and the test was CHANGED to accept the new value. The comment "small dev/on-device windows compact no later than before" (test comment) — keepRecent affects what's retained post-compaction, not the trigger. So keep halving at 16384 means after compaction less context is retained — a behavior change for small models. Not necessarily a bug, but it contradicts "byte-identical legacy behavior" claims? No — that claim was about pressure decision with no observation, not settings.

OK so this is a genuine doc-vs-code mismatch (comment claims parity band ≤64k; actual parity band is ≤16384 for reserve, and keep parity only ≤... let me compute keep crossover: legacy keep = min(200, max(2048, window/2)). New keep = min(131072, max(max(window/8,2048), min(4096, window/2)).

The child Agent doesn't get a `contextWindowCap` — the Agent class has no cap param presumably; the loop's guard reads `effectiveContextWindow(model.contextWindow, cap)` from its own config. For the child, the guard basis is `model.contextWindow` (cap = null, since the child loop config presumably has contextWindowCap null). So withRegisteredContextWindow puts the REGISTERED (uncapped) window on the child model — the child's over-window guard basis. Meanwhile `_compactChildIfNeeded` computes the compaction window as effectiveContextWindow(registry window, cap). If the owner cap RAISES... the cap can't raise above the registered window (cap raises above catalog but here the basis is already the registered/served window). If the cap clamps DOWN (cap < registered window), then: compaction basis = cap, guard basis = registered (uncapped). The guard fires later than compaction. Previously (before this PR): guard basis = model.contextWindow (catalog) and compaction basis = effectiveContextWindow(catalog, null) — consistent. Now with a registry entry + a clamp-down cap: compaction at 256k basis, guard at 1M. The compaction trigger (window−reserve at 256k) fires far before the guard at 1M — compaction is proactive anyway, so the guard lag is not harmful per se; guard is last resort. Actually wait, the inconsistency direction: compaction fires EARLIER than the guard. That's safe-ish (compaction is the mechanism; the guard is emergency). The comment in _resolveChildWiring claims "the child loop's over-window guard and the compaction threshold divide by the same honest number the main agent and the ctx meter resolve" — with a clamp-down cap they don't: guard rides the uncapped registered window, compaction the capped. Minor doc inaccuracy; behavior: compaction stays under the cap, guard lags — acceptable but the claim is inaccurate.

Hmm wait — actually which is "correct"? The owner cap says "treat the window as 256k" — the child compaction honors it (good, parity with main). The child guard sees 1M. If usage hits 300k (over the 256k cap), compaction should have fired at 240k (256k−16k). If compaction failed (best-effort), the guard wouldn't fire until 1M — riding way over the cap. Before the registry existed, guard = catalog 200k → guard fired at 200k. Now guard = registered 1M. Edge: registry publishes a raised window (endpoint report says 1M for a 200k-catalog id) + owner cap clamps to 256k + compaction repeatedly fails → the guard basis silently moved from 200k to 1M for children. The over-window guard is the "last resort" against provider hard-overflow; publishing a served-truth window SHOULD raise it (that's the point — the provider accepts 1M). But the owner explicitly capped at 256k — main's guard honors the cap (agent_loop uses cap), children's doesn't. So the child guard diverges from the main guard under a cap. That's a real, if edge-case, inconsistency: "the cap wins in whichever direction it points, same as the main agent" — for compaction, but NOT for the child loop guard (cap never reaches the child loop). Severity: IMPORTANT (edge case; compaction normally prevents reaching the guard).

If the line is ABOVE the legacy line, firing requires pressure > 192000 vs legacy pressure > 188416 — the new line fires LATER for a given pressure trajectory. The reason it doesn't fire later in this test is because pressure = max(est,obs) includes the observed channel that legacy didn't have. - window=8192: legacy reserve = min(16384, max(1024, 2048)) = 2048. New = min(65536, max(max(512,1024), min(4096,2048))) = max(1024, 2048) = 2048. Equal → parity.

- window=32768: legacy = 8192. New = max(2048, 4096) = 4096 → later. ✗
- window=49152: legacy = 12288. New = max(3072,4096)=4096 → later. ✗
- window=65536: legacy = 16384. New = max(4096,4096) = 4096 → later. ✗

The child Agent doesn't get a `contextWindowCap` — the Agent class has no cap param presumably; the loop's guard reads `effectiveContextWindow(model.contextWindow, cap)` from its own config. For the child, the guard basis is `model.contextWindow` (cap = null, since the child loop config presumably has contextWindowCap null). So withRegisteredContextWindow puts the REGISTERED (uncapped) window on the child model — the child's over-window guard basis. Meanwhile `_compactChildIfNeeded` computes the compaction window as effectiveContextWindow(registry window, cap). If the owner cap RAISES... the cap can't raise above the registered window (cap raises above catalog but here the basis is already the registered/served window). If the cap clamps DOWN (cap < registered window), then: compaction basis = cap, guard basis = registered (uncapped). The guard fires later than compaction. Previously (before this PR): guard basis = model.contextWindow (catalog) and compaction basis = effectiveContextWindow(catalog, null) — consistent. Now with a registry entry + a clamp-down cap: compaction at 256k basis, guard at 1M. The compaction trigger (window−reserve at 256k) fires far before the guard at 1M — compaction is proactive anyway, so the guard lag is not harmful per se; guard is last resort. Actually wait, the inconsistency direction: compaction fires EARLIER than the guard. That's safe-ish (compaction is the mechanism; the guard is emergency). The comment in _resolveChildWiring claims "the child loop's over-window guard and the compaction threshold divide by the same honest number the main agent and the ctx meter resolve" — with a clamp-down cap they don't: guard rides the uncapped registered window, compaction the capped. Minor doc inaccuracy; behavior: compaction stays under the cap, guard lags — acceptable but the claim is inaccurate.

Hmm wait — actually which is "correct"? The owner cap says "treat the window as 256k" — the child compaction honors it (good, parity with main). The child guard sees 1M. If usage hits 300k (over the 256k cap), compaction should have fired at 240k (256k−16k). If compaction failed (best-effort), the guard wouldn't fire until 1M — riding way over the cap. Before the registry existed, guard = catalog 200k → guard fired at 200k. Now guard = registered 1M. Edge: registry publishes a raised window (endpoint report says 1M for a 200k-catalog id) + owner cap clamps to 256k + compaction repeatedly fails → the guard basis silently moved from 200k to 1M for children. The over-window guard is the "last resort" against provider hard-overflow; publishing a served-truth window SHOULD raise it (that's the point — the provider accepts 1M). If the owner cap RAISES... the cap can't raise above the registered window (cap raises above catalog but here the basis is already the registered/served window). If the cap clamps DOWN (cap < registered window), then: compaction basis = cap, guard basis = registered (uncapped). The guard fires later than compaction. Previously (before this PR): guard basis = model.contextWindow (catalog) and compaction basis = effectiveContextWindow(catalog, null) — consistent. Now with a registry entry + a clamp-down cap: compaction at 256k basis, guard at 1M. The compaction trigger (window−reserve at 256k) fires far before the guard at 1M — compaction is proactive anyway, so the guard lag is not harmful per se; guard is last resort. Actually wait, the inconsistency direction: compaction fires EARLIER than the guard. That's safe-ish (compaction is the mechanism; the guard is emergency). The comment in _resolveChildWiring claims "the child loop's over-window guard and the compaction threshold divide by the same honest number the main agent and the ctx meter resolve" — with a clamp-down cap they don't: guard rides the uncapped registered window, compaction the capped. The child Agent doesn't get a `contextWindowCap` — the Agent class has no cap param presumably; the loop's guard reads `effectiveContextWindow(model.contextWindow, cap)` from its own config. For the child, the guard basis is `model.contextWindow` (cap = null, since the child loop config presumably has contextWindowCap null). So withRegisteredContextWindow puts the REGISTERED (uncapped) window on the child model — the child's over-window guard basis. Meanwhile `_compactChildIfNeeded` computes the compaction window as effectiveContextWindow(registry window, cap). If the owner cap RAISES... the cap can't raise above the registered window (cap raises above catalog but here the basis is already the registered/served window). If the cap clamps DOWN (cap < registered window), then: compaction basis = cap, guard basis = registered (uncapped). The guard fires later than compaction. Previously (before this PR): guard basis = model.contextWindow (catalog) and compaction basis = effectiveContextWindow(catalog, null) — consistent. Now with a registry entry + a clamp-down cap: compaction at 256k basis, guard at 1M. The compaction trigger (window−reserve at 256k) fires far before the guard at 1M — compaction is proactive anyway, so the guard lag is not harmful per se; guard is last resort. Actually wait, the inconsistency direction: compaction fires EARLIER than the guard. That's safe-ish (compaction is the mechanism; the guard is emergency). The comment in _resolveChildWiring claims "the child loop's over-window guard and the compaction threshold divide by the same honest number the main agent and the ctx meter resolve" — with a clamp-down cap they don't: guard rides the uncapped registered window, compaction the capped. Minor doc inaccuracy; behavior: compaction stays under the cap, guard lags — acceptable but the claim is inaccurate.

Hmm wait — actually which is "correct"? The owner cap says "treat the window as 256k" — the child compaction honors it (good, parity with main). The child guard sees 1M. If usage hits 300k (over the 256k cap), compaction should have fired at 240k (256k−16k). If compaction failed (best-effort), the guard wouldn't fire until 1M — riding way over the cap. The child Agent doesn't get a `contextWindowCap` — the Agent class has no cap param presumably; the loop's guard reads `effectiveContextWindow(model.contextWindow, cap)` from its own config. For the child, the guard basis is `model.contextWindow` (cap = null, since the child loop config presumably has contextWindowCap null). So withRegisteredContextWindow puts the REGISTERED (uncapped) window on the child model — the child's over-window guard basis. Meanwhile `_compactChildIfNeeded` computes the compaction window as effectiveContextWindow(registry window, cap). If the owner cap RAISES... the cap can't raise above the registered window (cap raises above catalog but here the basis is already the registered/served window). If the cap clamps DOWN (cap < registered window), then: compaction basis = cap, guard basis = registered (uncapped). The guard fires later than compaction. Previously (before this PR): guard basis = model.contextWindow (catalog) and compaction basis = effectiveContextWindow(catalog, null) — consistent. Now with a registry entry + a clamp-down cap: compaction at 256k basis, guard at 1M. The compaction trigger (window−reserve at 256k) fires far before the guard at 1M — compaction is proactive anyway, so the guard lag is not harmful per se; guard is last resort. Actually wait, the inconsistency direction: compaction fires EARLIER than the guard. That's safe-ish (compaction is the mechanism; the guard is emergency). The comment in _resolveChildWiring claims "the child loop's over-window guard and the compaction threshold divide by the same honest number the main agent and the ctx meter resolve" — with a clamp-down cap they don't: guard rides the uncapped registered window, compaction the capped. Hmm wait — actually which is "correct"? The owner cap says "treat the window as 256k" — the child compaction honors it (good, parity with main). The child guard sees 1M. If usage hits 300k (over the 256k cap), compaction should have fired at 240k (256k−16k). If compaction failed (best-effort), the guard wouldn't fire until 1M — riding way over the cap. Before the registry existed, guard = catalog 200k → guard fired at 200k. Now guard = registered 1M. Edge: registry publishes a raised window (endpoint report says 1M for a 200k-catalog id) + owner cap clamps to 256k + compaction repeatedly fails → the guard basis silently moved from 200k to 1M for children. The over-window guard is the "last resort" against provider hard-overflow; publishing a served-truth window SHOULD raise it (that's the point — the provider accepts 1M). But the owner explicitly capped at 256k — main's guard honors the cap (agent_loop uses cap), children's doesn't. So the child guard diverges from the main guard under a cap. That's a real, if edge-case, inconsistency: "the cap wins in whichever direction it points, same as the main agent" — for compaction, but NOT for the child loop guard (cap never reaches the child loop). arguments.content:
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the "≤64k fires no later than legacy" parity claim is not what the formula delivers**

This comment (and the mirrored test comment in `test/compaction/compaction_test.dart` "small dev/on-device windows compact no later than before", and the PR description) promises that the legacy-parity floor `min(4096, window ~/ 4)` keeps the ≤64k band firing **no later than before**. Executed against the actual formula, the parity band is only **≤16,384 and ≥262,144** — every window in between now compacts **later** than legacy on the estimate channel:

| window | new reserve | legacy reserve | new trigger | legacy trigger |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 20,480 | 4,096 | 5,120 | 16,384 | 15,360 |
| 32,768 | 4,096 | 8,192 | 28,672 | 24,576 |
| 65,536 | 4,096 | 16,384 | 61,440 | 49,152 |
| 131,072 | 8,192 | 16,384 | 122,880 | 114,688 |
| 200,000 | 12,500 | 16,384 | 187,500 | 183,616 |

The legacy reserve ramped as `window ~/ 4` up to a 16,384 cap; the new floor caps the parity term at **4,096**, so it stops matching legacy at 16,384 — not at 65,536 where the proportional term takes over. The "fades out exactly where the proportional term takes over" reasoning is off by exactly that gap.

Impact: for the whole (16k, 262k) band — i.e. most hosted sessions (128k/200k windows) — a provider that reports no usable usage (the E1 degradation path this same PR documents as "estimate-only, exactly the legacy behavior") now rides 4k–12k tokens closer to the hard window than the legacy behavior the claim promises to preserve, with no observed channel as backstop. With usage reporting the forced observed channel covers it (that is what REG-1 pins), so this is bounded drift, not breakage — but either the guarantee or the formula should be true.

Please pick one:

{"path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment1.md","content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the "≤64k fires no later than legacy" parity claim is not what the formula delivers**

This comment (and the mirrored test comment in `test/compaction/compaction_test.dart` "small dev/on-device windows compact no later than before", and the PR description) promises that the legacy-parity floor `min(4096, window ~/ 4)` keeps the ≤64k band firing **no later than before**. Executed against the actual formula, the parity band is only **≤16,384 and ≥262,144** — every window in between now compacts **later** than legacy on the estimate channel:

| window | new reserve | legacy reserve | new trigger | legacy trigger |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 20,480 | 4,096 | 5,120 | 16,384 | 15,360 |
| 32,768 | 4,096 | 8,192 | 28,672 | 24,576 |
| 65,536 | 4,096 | 16,384 | 61,440 | 49,152 |
| 131,072 | 8,192 | 16,384 | 122,880 | 114,688 |
| 200,000 | 12,500 | 16,384 | 187,500 | 183,616 |

The legacy reserve ramped as `window ~/ 4` up to a 16,384 cap; the new floor caps the parity term at **4,096**, so it stops matching legacy at 16,384 — not at 65,536 where the proportional term takes over. The "fades out exactly where the proportional term takes over" reasoning is off by exactly that gap.

Impact: for the whole (16k, 262k) band — i.e. most hosted sessions (128k/200k windows) — a provider that reports no usable usage (the E1 degradation path this same PR documents as "estimate-only, exactly the legacy behavior") now rides 4k–12k tokens closer to the hard window than the legacy behavior the claim promises to preserve, with no observed channel as backstop. With usage reporting the forced observed channel covers it (that is what REG-1 pins), so this is bounded drift, not breakage — but either the guarantee or the formula should be true.

Please pick one:
- widen the floor to `min(16384, window ~/ 4)` (exact legacy parity below 262,144, proportional above — `max(window ~/ 16, min(16384, window ~/ 4))`), or
- correct this comment, the test comment, and the PR description to state the real crossover (≤16,384 / ≥262,144) and add a table row in `UT-2` pinning one mid-band window (e.g. `forWindow(32768).reserveTokens == 4096`) so the drift is documented instead of implicit.

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the child loop guard rides the UNCAPPED registered window while child compaction rides the capped one**

`_resolveChildWiring` stamps the REGISTERED (uncapped) window onto the child `Model` via `withRegisteredContextWindow`, and this doc comment says the child loop's over-window guard and the compaction threshold now "divide by the same honest number". They do only when no clamp-down owner cap is set:

- compaction basis: `_childContextWindow` → `effectiveContextWindow(registry window, contextWindowCap)` — capped ✓
- guard basis: the child `Agent` is built in `_buildChild` **without** `contextWindowCap` (the `Agent`/`AgentLoopConfig` parameter exists, `agent.dart:214`), so the guard computes `effectiveContextWindow(childModel.contextWindow, null)` → the uncapped registered value ✗

Concretely: registry publishes 1M for a 200k-catalog id, owner sets `agent.contextWindowCap: 256000` → child compaction fires at the 256k basis, but the child's over-window guard (and the gh-1409 operative-pin budget at `agent_loop.dart:1715`, same formula) measure against 1M. Before this PR both bases were the catalog window, so they agreed; the registry raise is what forks them. If compaction repeatedly fails (it is best-effort by contract — "the over-window guard stays the last resort"), the last resort now trips ~744k tokens later than the owner's cap intends, and the main agent's guard (which does honor the cap) diverges from its own children's.

Fix is one line — pass the cap into the child agent so every child-side consumer shares the capped basis:

```dart
final child = Agent(
  model: wiring.model,
  contextWindowCap: contextWindowCap, // gh-1742: same clamp the main loop runs
  ...
);
```

(or apply the cap inside `withRegisteredContextWindow` at the wiring site — but then `_childContextWindow` and the guard must keep agreeing by construction, so the constructor param is the safer single clamp point).

{"path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment1.md","content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the "≤64k fires no later than legacy" parity claim is not what the formula delivers**

This comment (and the mirrored test comment in `test/compaction/compaction_test.dart` "small dev/on-device windows compact no later than before", and the PR description) promises that the legacy-parity floor `min(4096, window ~/ 4)` keeps the ≤64k band firing **no later than before**. Executed against the actual formula, the parity band is only **≤16,384 and ≥262,144** — every window in between now compacts **later** than legacy on the estimate channel:

| window | new reserve | legacy reserve | new trigger | legacy trigger |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 20,480 | 4,096 | 5,120 | 16,384 | 15,360 |
| 32,768 | 4,096 | 8,192 | 28,672 | 24,576 |
| 65,536 | 4,096 | 16,384 | 61,440 | 49,152 |
| 131,072 | 8,192 | 16,384 | 122,880 | 114,688 |
| 200,000 | 12,500 | 16,384 | 187,500 | 183,616 |

The legacy reserve ramped as `window ~/ 4` up to a 16,384 cap; the new floor caps the parity term at **4,096**, so it stops matching legacy at 16,384 — not at 65,536 where the proportional term takes over. The "fades out exactly where the proportional term takes over" reasoning is off by exactly that gap.

Impact: for the whole (16k, 262k) band — i.e. most hosted sessions (128k/200k windows) — a provider that reports no usable usage (the E1 degradation path this same PR documents as "estimate-only, exactly the legacy behavior") now rides 4k–12k tokens closer to the hard window than the legacy behavior the claim promises to preserve, with no observed channel as backstop. With usage reporting the forced observed channel covers it (that is what REG-1 pins), so this is bounded drift, not breakage — but either the guarantee or the formula should be true.

Please pick one:
- widen the floor to `min(16384, window ~/ 4)` (exact legacy parity below 262,144, proportional above — `max(window ~/ 16, min(16384, window ~/ 4))`), or
- correct this comment, the test comment, and the PR description to state the real crossover (≤16,384 / ≥262,144) and add a table row in `UT-2` pinning one mid-band window (e.g. `forWindow(32768).reserveTokens == 4096`) so the drift is documented instead of implicit.

{"content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the child loop guard rides the UNCAPPED registered window while child compaction rides the capped one**

`_resolveChildWiring` stamps the REGISTERED (uncapped) window onto the child `Model` via `withRegisteredContextWindow`, and this doc comment says the child loop's over-window guard and the compaction threshold now "divide by the same honest number". They do only when no clamp-down owner cap is set:

- compaction basis: `_childContextWindow` → `effectiveContextWindow(registry window, contextWindowCap)` — capped ✓
- guard basis: the child `Agent` is built in `_buildChild` **without** `contextWindowCap` (the `Agent`/`AgentLoopConfig` parameter exists, `agent.dart:214`), so the guard computes `effectiveContextWindow(childModel.contextWindow, null)` → the uncapped registered value ✗

Concretely: registry publishes 1M for a 200k-catalog id, owner sets `agent.contextWindowCap: 256000` → child compaction fires at the 256k basis, but the child's over-window guard (and the gh-1409 operative-pin budget at `agent_loop.dart:1715`, same formula) measure against 1M. Before this PR both bases were the catalog window, so they agreed; the registry raise is what forks them. If compaction repeatedly fails (it is best-effort by contract — "the over-window guard stays the last resort"), the last resort now trips ~744k tokens later than the owner's cap intends, and the main agent's guard (which does honor the cap) diverges from its own children's.

Fix is one line — pass the cap into the child agent so every child-side consumer shares the capped basis:

```dart
final child = Agent(
  model: wiring.model,
  contextWindowCap: contextWindowCap, // gh-1742: same clamp the main loop runs
  ...
);
```

(or apply the cap inside `withRegisteredContextWindow` at the wiring site — but then `_childContextWindow` and the guard must keep agreeing by construction, so the constructor param is the safer single clamp point).

💡 **SUGGESTION: `hasAnyReportedUsage` is exported but has no caller**

`hasAnyReportedUsage` is barrel-exported public API, but nothing in `lib/` calls it — only its own test does. Its doc justifies it via E1 ("worth the caller's once-per-model note"), but that once-per-model note is not implemented anywhere in this PR (neither the executor nor the CLI stamps a "this provider never reports usage" hint anywhere).

Two options:
- wire the consumer this PR's doc promises (e.g. a one-time dim line when a child ran ≥N boundaries estimate-only while a registry entry marked the window verified — the exact gh-112 confusion shape), or
- keep the function but drop it from the barrel until a caller exists, so the public API surface (gh-1232 append-only policy) doesn't grow a speculative export.

Not blocking — dead-but-tested public helpers are cheap — but the barrel is append-only by policy, so exporting before the consumer exists is the wrong order.

{"path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment1.md","content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the "≤64k fires no later than legacy" parity claim is not what the formula delivers**

This comment (and the mirrored test comment in `test/compaction/compaction_test.dart` "small dev/on-device windows compact no later than before", and the PR description) promises that the legacy-parity floor `min(4096, window ~/ 4)` keeps the ≤64k band firing **no later than before**. Executed against the actual formula, the parity band is only **≤16,384 and ≥262,144** — every window in between now compacts **later** than legacy on the estimate channel:

| window | new reserve | legacy reserve | new trigger | legacy trigger |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 20,480 | 4,096 | 5,120 | 16,384 | 15,360 |
| 32,768 | 4,096 | 8,192 | 28,672 | 24,576 |
| 65,536 | 4,096 | 16,384 | 61,440 | 49,152 |
| 131,072 | 8,192 | 16,384 | 122,880 | 114,688 |
| 200,000 | 12,500 | 16,384 | 187,500 | 183,616 |

The legacy reserve ramped as `window ~/ 4` up to a 16,384 cap; the new floor caps the parity term at **4,096**, so it stops matching legacy at 16,384 — not at 65,536 where the proportional term takes over. The "fades out exactly where the proportional term takes over" reasoning is off by exactly that gap.

Impact: for the whole (16k, 262k) band — i.e. most hosted sessions (128k/200k windows) — a provider that reports no usable usage (the E1 degradation path this same PR documents as "estimate-only, exactly the legacy behavior") now rides 4k–12k tokens closer to the hard window than the legacy behavior the claim promises to preserve, with no observed channel as backstop. With usage reporting the forced observed channel covers it (that is what REG-1 pins), so this is bounded drift, not breakage — but either the guarantee or the formula should be true.

Please pick one:
- widen the floor to `min(16384, window ~/ 4)` (exact legacy parity below 262,144, proportional above — `max(window ~/ 16, min(16384, window ~/ 4))`), or
- correct this comment, the test comment, and the PR description to state the real crossover (≤16,384 / ≥262,144) and add a table row in `UT-2` pinning one mid-band window (e.g. `forWindow(32768).reserveTokens == 4096`) so the drift is documented instead of implicit.

{"content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the child loop guard rides the UNCAPPED registered window while child compaction rides the capped one**

`_resolveChildWiring` stamps the REGISTERED (uncapped) window onto the child `Model` via `withRegisteredContextWindow`, and this doc comment says the child loop's over-window guard and the compaction threshold now "divide by the same honest number". They do only when no clamp-down owner cap is set:

- compaction basis: `_childContextWindow` → `effectiveContextWindow(registry window, contextWindowCap)` — capped ✓
- guard basis: the child `Agent` is built in `_buildChild` **without** `contextWindowCap` (the `Agent`/`AgentLoopConfig` parameter exists, `agent.dart:214`), so the guard computes `effectiveContextWindow(childModel.contextWindow, null)` → the uncapped registered value ✗

Concretely: registry publishes 1M for a 200k-catalog id, owner sets `agent.contextWindowCap: 256000` → child compaction fires at the 256k basis, but the child's over-window guard (and the gh-1409 operative-pin budget at `agent_loop.dart:1715`, same formula) measure against 1M. Before this PR both bases were the catalog window, so they agreed; the registry raise is what forks them. If compaction repeatedly fails (it is best-effort by contract — "the over-window guard stays the last resort"), the last resort now trips ~744k tokens later than the owner's cap intends, and the main agent's guard (which does honor the cap) diverges from its own children's.

Fix is one line — pass the cap into the child agent so every child-side consumer shares the capped basis:

```dart
final child = Agent(
  model: wiring.model,
  contextWindowCap: contextWindowCap, // gh-1742: same clamp the main loop runs
  ...
);
```

(or apply the cap inside `withRegisteredContextWindow` at the wiring site — but then `_childContextWindow` and the guard must keep agreeing by construction, so the constructor param is the safer single clamp point).

{"path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment1.md","content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the "≤64k fires no later than legacy" parity claim is not what the formula delivers**

This comment (and the mirrored test comment in `test/compaction/compaction_test.dart` "small dev/on-device windows compact no later than before", and the PR description) promises that the legacy-parity floor `min(4096, window ~/ 4)` keeps the ≤64k band firing **no later than before**. Executed against the actual formula, the parity band is only **≤16,384 and ≥262,144** — every window in between now compacts **later** than legacy on the estimate channel:

| window | new reserve | legacy reserve | new trigger | legacy trigger |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 20,480 | 4,096 | 5,120 | 16,384 | 15,360 |
| 32,768 | 4,096 | 8,192 | 28,672 | 24,576 |
| 65,536 | 4,096 | 16,384 | 61,440 | 49,152 |
| 131,072 | 8,192 | 16,384 | 122,880 | 114,688 |
| 200,000 | 12,500 | 16,384 | 187,500 | 183,616 |

The legacy reserve ramped as `window ~/ 4` up to a 16,384 cap; the new floor caps the parity term at **4,096**, so it stops matching legacy at 16,384 — not at 65,536 where the proportional term takes over. The "fades out exactly where the proportional term takes over" reasoning is off by exactly that gap.

Impact: for the whole (16k, 262k) band — i.e. most hosted sessions (128k/200k windows) — a provider that reports no usable usage (the E1 degradation path this same PR documents as "estimate-only, exactly the legacy behavior") now rides 4k–12k tokens closer to the hard window than the legacy behavior the claim promises to preserve, with no observed channel as backstop. With usage reporting the forced observed channel covers it (that is what REG-1 pins), so this is bounded drift, not breakage — but either the guarantee or the formula should be true.

Please pick one:
- widen the floor to `min(16384, window ~/ 4)` (exact legacy parity below 262,144, proportional above — `max(window ~/ 16, min(16384, window ~/ 4))`), or
- correct this comment, the test comment, and the PR description to state the real crossover (≤16,384 / ≥262,144) and add a table row in `UT-2` pinning one mid-band window (e.g. `forWindow(32768).reserveTokens == 4096`) so the drift is documented instead of implicit.

{"content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the child loop guard rides the UNCAPPED registered window while child compaction rides the capped one**

`_resolveChildWiring` stamps the REGISTERED (uncapped) window onto the child `Model` via `withRegisteredContextWindow`, and this doc comment says the child loop's over-window guard and the compaction threshold now "divide by the same honest number". They do only when no clamp-down owner cap is set:

- compaction basis: `_childContextWindow` → `effectiveContextWindow(registry window, contextWindowCap)` — capped ✓
- guard basis: the child `Agent` is built in `_buildChild` **without** `contextWindowCap` (the `Agent`/`AgentLoopConfig` parameter exists, `agent.dart:214`), so the guard computes `effectiveContextWindow(childModel.contextWindow, null)` → the uncapped registered value ✗

Concretely: registry publishes 1M for a 200k-catalog id, owner sets `agent.contextWindowCap: 256000` → child compaction fires at the 256k basis, but the child's over-window guard (and the gh-1409 operative-pin budget at `agent_loop.dart:1715`, same formula) measure against 1M. Before this PR both bases were the catalog window, so they agreed; the registry raise is what forks them. If compaction repeatedly fails (it is best-effort by contract — "the over-window guard stays the last resort"), the last resort now trips ~744k tokens later than the owner's cap intends, and the main agent's guard (which does honor the cap) diverges from its own children's.

Fix is one line — pass the cap into the child agent so every child-side consumer shares the capped basis:

```dart
final child = Agent(
  model: wiring.model,
  contextWindowCap: contextWindowCap, // gh-1742: same clamp the main loop runs
  ...
);
```

(or apply the cap inside `withRegisteredContextWindow` at the wiring site — but then `_childContextWindow` and the guard must keep agreeing by construction, so the constructor param is the safer single clamp point).

{"path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment1.md","content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the "≤64k fires no later than legacy" parity claim is not what the formula delivers**

This comment (and the mirrored test comment in `test/compaction/compaction_test.dart` "small dev/on-device windows compact no later than before", and the PR description) promises that the legacy-parity floor `min(4096, window ~/ 4)` keeps the ≤64k band firing **no later than before**. Executed against the actual formula, the parity band is only **≤16,384 and ≥262,144** — every window in between now compacts **later** than legacy on the estimate channel:

| window | new reserve | legacy reserve | new trigger | legacy trigger |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 20,480 | 4,096 | 5,120 | 16,384 | 15,360 |
| 32,768 | 4,096 | 8,192 | 28,672 | 24,576 |
| 65,536 | 4,096 | 16,384 | 61,440 | 49,152 |
| 131,072 | 8,192 | 16,384 | 122,880 | 114,688 |
| 200,000 | 12,500 | 16,384 | 187,500 | 183,616 |

The legacy reserve ramped as `window ~/ 4` up to a 16,384 cap; the new floor caps the parity term at **4,096**, so it stops matching legacy at 16,384 — not at 65,536 where the proportional term takes over. The "fades out exactly where the proportional term takes over" reasoning is off by exactly that gap.

Impact: for the whole (16k, 262k) band — i.e. most hosted sessions (128k/200k windows) — a provider that reports no usable usage (the E1 degradation path this same PR documents as "estimate-only, exactly the legacy behavior") now rides 4k–12k tokens closer to the hard window than the legacy behavior the claim promises to preserve, with no observed channel as backstop. With usage reporting the forced observed channel covers it (that is what REG-1 pins), so this is bounded drift, not breakage — but either the guarantee or the formula should be true.

Please pick one:
- widen the floor to `min(16384, window ~/ 4)` (exact legacy parity below 262,144, proportional above — `max(window ~/ 16, min(16384, window ~/ 4))`), or
- correct this comment, the test comment, and the PR description to state the real crossover (≤16,384 / ≥262,144) and add a table row in `UT-2` pinning one mid-band window (e.g. `forWindow(32768).reserveTokens == 4096`) so the drift is documented instead of implicit.
"}

{"content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the child loop guard rides the UNCAPPED registered window while child compaction rides the capped one**

`_resolveChildWiring` stamps the REGISTERED (uncapped) window onto the child `Model` via `withRegisteredContextWindow`, and this doc comment says the child loop's over-window guard and the compaction threshold now "divide by the same honest number". They do only when no clamp-down owner cap is set:

- compaction basis: `_childContextWindow` → `effectiveContextWindow(registry window, contextWindowCap)` — capped ✓
- guard basis: the child `Agent` is built in `_buildChild` **without** `contextWindowCap` (the `Agent`/`AgentLoopConfig` parameter exists, `agent.dart:214`), so the guard computes `effectiveContextWindow(childModel.contextWindow, null)` → the uncapped registered value ✗

Concretely: registry publishes 1M for a 200k-catalog id, owner sets `agent.contextWindowCap: 256000` → child compaction fires at the 256k basis, but the child's over-window guard (and the gh-1409 operative-pin budget at `agent_loop.dart:1715`, same formula) measure against 1M. Before this PR both bases were the catalog window, so they agreed; the registry raise is what forks them. If compaction repeatedly fails (it is best-effort by contract — "the over-window guard stays the last resort"), the last resort now trips ~744k tokens later than the owner's cap intends, and the main agent's guard (which does honor the cap) diverges from its own children's.

Fix is one line — pass the cap into the child agent so every child-side consumer shares the capped basis:

```dart
final child = Agent(
  model: wiring.model,
  contextWindowCap: contextWindowCap, // gh-1742: same clamp the main loop runs
  ...
);
```

(or apply the cap inside `withRegisteredContextWindow` at the wiring site — but then `_childContextWindow` and the guard must keep agreeing by construction, so the constructor param is the safer single clamp point).

{"content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: second hand-rolled Model copy — consider one shared helper**

{"path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment1.md","content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the "≤64k fires no later than legacy" parity claim is not what the formula delivers**

This comment (and the mirrored test comment in `test/compaction/compaction_test.dart` "small dev/on-device windows compact no later than before", and the PR description) promises that the legacy-parity floor `min(4096, window ~/ 4)` keeps the ≤64k band firing **no later than before**. Executed against the actual formula, the parity band is only **≤16,384 and ≥262,144** — every window in between now compacts **later** than legacy on the estimate channel:

| window | new reserve | legacy reserve | new trigger | legacy trigger |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 20,480 | 4,096 | 5,120 | 16,384 | 15,360 |
| 32,768 | 4,096 | 8,192 | 28,672 | 24,576 |
| 65,536 | 4,096 | 16,384 | 61,440 | 49,152 |
| 131,072 | 8,192 | 16,384 | 122,880 | 114,688 |
| 200,000 | 12,500 | 16,384 | 187,500 | 183,616 |

The legacy reserve ramped as `window ~/ 4` up to a 16,384 cap; the new floor caps the parity term at **4,096**, so it stops matching legacy at 16,384 — not at 65,536 where the proportional term takes over. The "fades out exactly where the proportional term takes over" reasoning is off by exactly that gap.

Impact: for the whole (16k, 262k) band — i.e. most hosted sessions (128k/200k windows) — a provider that reports no usable usage (the E1 degradation path this same PR documents as "estimate-only, exactly the legacy behavior") now rides 4k–12k tokens closer to the hard window than the legacy behavior the claim promises to preserve, with no observed channel as backstop. With usage reporting the forced observed channel covers it (that is what REG-1 pins), so this is bounded drift, not breakage — but either the guarantee or the formula should be true.

Please pick one:
- widen the floor to `min(16384, window ~/ 4)` (exact legacy parity below 262,144, proportional above — `max(window ~/ 16, min(16384, window ~/ 4))`), or
- correct this comment, the test comment, and the PR description to state the real crossover (≤16,384 / ≥262,144) and add a table row in `UT-2` pinning one mid-band window (e.g. `forWindow(32768).reserveTokens == 4096`) so the drift is documented instead of implicit.

{"content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the child loop guard rides the UNCAPPED registered window while child compaction rides the capped one**

`_resolveChildWiring` stamps the REGISTERED (uncapped) window onto the child `Model` via `withRegisteredContextWindow`, and this doc comment says the child loop's over-window guard and the compaction threshold now "divide by the same honest number". They do only when no clamp-down owner cap is set:

- compaction basis: `_childContextWindow` → `effectiveContextWindow(registry window, contextWindowCap)` — capped ✓
- guard basis: the child `Agent` is built in `_buildChild` **without** `contextWindowCap` (the `Agent`/`AgentLoopConfig` parameter exists, `agent.dart:214`), so the guard computes `effectiveContextWindow(childModel.contextWindow, null)` → the uncapped registered value ✗

Concretely: registry publishes 1M for a 200k-catalog id, owner sets `agent.contextWindowCap: 256000` → child compaction fires at the 256k basis, but the child's over-window guard (and the gh-1409 operative-pin budget at `agent_loop.dart:1715`, same formula) measure against 1M. Before this PR both bases were the catalog window, so they agreed; the registry raise is what forks them. If compaction repeatedly fails (it is best-effort by contract — "the over-window guard stays the last resort"), the last resort now trips ~744k tokens later than the owner's cap intends, and the main agent's guard (which does honor the cap) diverges from its own children's.

Fix is one line — pass the cap into the child agent so every child-side consumer shares the capped basis:

```dart
final child = Agent(
  model: wiring.model,
  contextWindowCap: contextWindowCap, // gh-1742: same clamp the main loop runs
  ...
);
```

(or apply the cap inside `withRegisteredContextWindow` at the wiring site — but then `_childContextWindow` and the guard must keep agreeing by construction, so the constructor param is the safer single clamp point).

This comment (and the mirrored test comment in `test/compaction/compaction_test.dart` "small dev/on-device windows compact no later than before", and the PR description) promises that the legacy-parity floor `min(4096, window ~/ 4)` keeps the ≤64k band firing **no later than before**. Executed against the actual formula, the parity band is only **≤16,384 and ≥262,144** — every window in between now compacts **later** than legacy on the estimate channel:

| window | new reserve | legacy reserve | new trigger | legacy trigger |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 20,480 | 4,096 | 5,120 | 16,384 | 15,360 |
| 32,768 | 4,096 | 8,192 | 28,672 | 24,576 |
| 65,536 | 4,096 | 16,384 | 61,440 | 49,152 |
| 131,072 | 8,192 | 16,384 | 122,880 | 114,688 |
| 200,000 | 12,500 | 16,384 | 187,500 | 183,616 |

The legacy reserve ramped as `window ~/ 4` up to a 16,384 cap; the new floor caps the parity term at **4,096**, so it stops matching legacy at 16,384 — not at 65,536 where the proportional term takes over. The "fades out exactly where the proportional term takes over" reasoning is off by exactly that gap.

Impact: for the whole (16k, 262k) band — i.e. most hosted sessions (128k/200k windows) — a provider that reports no usable usage (the E1 degradation path this same PR documents as "estimate-only, exactly the legacy behavior") now rides 4k–12k tokens closer to the hard window than the legacy behavior the claim promises to preserve, with no observed channel as backstop. With usage reporting the forced observed channel covers it (that is what REG-1 pins), so this is bounded drift, not breakage — but either the guarantee or the formula should be true.

Please pick one:
- widen the floor to `min(16384, window ~/ 4)` (exact legacy parity below 262,144, proportional above — `max(window ~/ 16, min(16384, window ~/ 4))`), or
- correct this comment, the test comment, and the PR description to state the real crossover (≤16,384 / ≥262,144) and add a table row in `UT-2` pinning one mid-band window (e.g. `forWindow(32768).reserveTokens == 4096`) so the drift is documented instead of implicit.

{"content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the child loop guard rides the UNCAPPED registered window while child compaction rides the capped one**

`_resolveChildWiring` stamps the REGISTERED (uncapped) window onto the child `Model` via `withRegisteredContextWindow`, and this doc comment says the child loop's over-window guard and the compaction threshold now "divide by the same honest number". They do only when no clamp-down owner cap is set:

- compaction basis: `_childContextWindow` → `effectiveContextWindow(registry window, contextWindowCap)` — capped ✓
- guard basis: the child `Agent` is built in `_buildChild` **without** `contextWindowCap` (the `Agent`/`AgentLoopConfig` parameter exists, `agent.dart:214`), so the guard computes `effectiveContextWindow(childModel.contextWindow, null)` → the uncapped registered value ✗

Concretely: registry publishes 1M for a 200k-catalog id, owner sets `agent.contextWindowCap: 256000` → child compaction fires at the 256k basis, but the child's over-window guard (and the gh-1409 operative-pin budget at `agent_loop.dart:1715`, same formula) measure against 1M. Before this PR both bases were the catalog window, so they agreed; the registry raise is what forks them. If compaction repeatedly fails (it is best-effort by contract — "the over-window guard stays the last resort"), the last resort now trips ~744k tokens later than the owner's cap intends, and the main agent's guard (which does honor the cap) diverges from its own children's.

Fix is one line — pass the cap into the child agent so every child-side consumer shares the capped basis:

```dart
final child = Agent(
  model: wiring.model,
  contextWindowCap: contextWindowCap, // gh-1742: same clamp the main loop runs
  ...
);
```

(or apply the cap inside `withRegisteredContextWindow` at the wiring site — but then `_childContextWindow` and the guard must keep agreeing by construction, so the constructor param is the safer single clamp point).

{"path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment1.md","content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the "≤64k fires no later than legacy" parity claim is not what the formula delivers**

This comment (and the mirrored test comment in `test/compaction/compaction_test.dart` "small dev/on-device windows compact no later than before", and the PR description) promises that the legacy-parity floor `min(4096, window ~/ 4)` keeps the ≤64k band firing **no later than before**. Executed against the actual formula, the parity band is only **≤16,384 and ≥262,144** — every window in between now compacts **later** than legacy on the estimate channel:

| window | new reserve | legacy reserve | new trigger | legacy trigger |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 20,480 | 4,096 | 5,120 | 16,384 | 15,360 |
| 32,768 | 4,096 | 8,192 | 28,672 | 24,576 |
| 65,536 | 4,096 | 16,384 | 61,440 | 49,152 |
| 131,072 | 8,192 | 16,384 | 122,880 | 114,688 |
| 200,000 | 12,500 | 16,384 | 187,500 | 183,616 |

The legacy reserve ramped as `window ~/ 4` up to a 16,384 cap; the new floor caps the parity term at **4,096**, so it stops matching legacy at 16,384 — not at 65,536 where the proportional term takes over. The "fades out exactly where the proportional term takes over" reasoning is off by exactly that gap.

Impact: for the whole (16k, 262k) band — i.e. most hosted sessions (128k/200k windows) — a provider that reports no usable usage (the E1 degradation path this same PR documents as "estimate-only, exactly the legacy behavior") now rides 4k–12k tokens closer to the hard window than the legacy behavior the claim promises to preserve, with no observed channel as backstop. With usage reporting the forced observed channel covers it (that is what REG-1 pins), so this is bounded drift, not breakage — but either the guarantee or the formula should be true.

Please pick one:
- widen the floor to `min(16384, window ~/ 4)` (exact legacy parity below 262,144, proportional above — `max(window ~/ 16, min(16384, window ~/ 4))`), or
- correct this comment, the test comment, and the PR description to state the real crossover (≤16,384 / ≥262,144) and add a table row in `UT-2` pinning one mid-band window (e.g. `forWindow(32768).reserveTokens == 4096`) so the drift is documented instead of implicit.
"}
